rationale: It gives log N(𝔭) exactly when the ideal is 𝔭^k with 𝔭 prime in the monoid of ideals (a nonzero prime ideal) and k ≥ 1, and 0 otherwise, which is the classical ideal von Mangoldt function. The choice in h.choose is harmless because ideal factorisation in 𝓞 K is unique, and the unit ideal gets 0 (vonMangoldt_one). Test mark made while setting up this repository.

checks: a prime ideal P gets log N(P)
every positive power P^n also gets log N(P), not log N(P^n), which is what separates it from log N
it vanishes exactly on the ideals that are not prime powers
a finite set of primes has density 0
a set has at most one density: it is a limit, not a limit point
the complement of a set of density δ has density 1 − δ
it agrees with Dirichlet density whenever it exists
as a function it is the Hecke slash sum over the double coset
given coset representatives a_i of the double coset, it is the classical sum of the slashes f |[k] a_i

about: the residue theorem for contours passing *through* poles (under mild crossing regularity): the integral becomes a principal value, the winding number a generalized one taking non-integer values on the contour.
name: The Hungerbühler–Wasem generalized residue theorem

about: (Hungerbühler–Wasem Def 2.1), with their real bounded-integrand formula Prop 2.3.
name: The generalized winding number

about: the contour integral of `f'/f` counts zeros minus poles, weighted by winding number.
name: The argument principle

about: the integral of a holomorphic function over a cycle null-homologous in the domain vanishes.
name: The homology form of Cauchy's theorem

about: the decay estimate for semicircular arcs in Fourier-type residue evaluations.
name: Jordan's lemma

about: every simply connected proper open subset of `ℂ` is biholomorphic to the unit disc, uniquely after normalisation.
name: The Riemann mapping theorem

about: two holomorphic functions differing by less than `|f|` on a circle have the same number of zeros inside it.
name: Rouché's theorem

about: a locally uniform limit of nowhere-vanishing holomorphic functions is nowhere vanishing or identically zero.
name: Hurwitz's theorem

about: a locally bounded sequence of holomorphic functions has a locally uniformly convergent subsequence.
name: Montel's selection theorem

about: a locally bounded sequence converging on a set with a limit point converges locally uniformly on the whole connected domain.
name: Vitali's convergence theorem

about: across the real axis, an affine line, a circle, and an analytic arc.
name: The Schwarz reflection principle

about: a holomorphic self-map of the disc does not increase the hyperbolic metric; with the hyperbolic triangle inequality.
name: The infinitesimal Schwarz–Pick inequality

about: an exchangeable sequence is a mixture of i.i.d. sequences, with contractable ⟺ exchangeable ⟺ mixed i.i.d.
name: The de Finetti–Ryll-Nardzewski theorem

about: an exchangeable event for an i.i.d. sequence has probability 0 or 1.
name: The Hewitt–Savage zero-one law

about: for an antitone filtration `𝔽`, the conditional expectations `μ[f | 𝔽 n]` converge a.e. to the conditional expectation given the intersection σ-algebra, complementing Mathlib's upward theorem.
name: Lévy's downward theorem

about: the random measure an exchangeable sequence is conditionally i.i.d. on, with its mixture identity.
name: The directing measure

about: the Hermite functions diagonalise the Fourier transform, in the rescaling matched to Mathlib's `exp(-2πixξ)` convention.
name: Hermite functions as Fourier eigenfunctions

about: nonnegative with completely monotone derivative, with their relation to completely monotone functions.
name: Bernstein functions

about: the two-sided comparison of a nonnegative harmonic function with its centre value, and the pairwise form with sharp constant `((R+r)/(R−r))²`.
name: Harnack's inequality on a planar disk

about: from a Maschke/Artin–Wedderburn presentation of `k[G]` as a product of matrix algebras: `∑ nᵢ² = |G|`, and the block count is the number of conjugacy classes.
name: The Wedderburn blocks of a finite group algebra

about: with inversion sets and the permutation action.
name: Generation of the Weyl group by simple reflections

about: the grading formulas underlying grid homology, invariant under grid reflection and half-turn rotation.
name: The Maslov and Alexander gradings for grid states

about: analytic continuation of a germ along the paths of a homotopy rel endpoints always ends in the same germ, with the null-homotopic-loop corollary; proved via a perturbation-stability argument, with continuation along a path itself defined in TauCeti#1523. Mathlib carries an abstract path-lifting form; this is the analytic-continuation statement.
name: The monodromy theorem

about: every finite-dimensional continuous representation of a compact group admits an invariant inner product by Haar averaging, hence is unitarizable.
name: Weyl's unitarian trick

about: an indecomposable module of finite length has a local endomorphism ring, the key input to Krull–Schmidt; Mathlib carries the noetherian Fitting decomposition this builds on.
name: Fitting's lemma

about: a finite-dimensional central simple algebra is a matrix algebra over a **central** division algebra, sharpening the division-algebra form.
name: Wedderburn–Artin for central simple algebras

about: the character identity `⟨χ_{Ind f}, χ⟩_G = ⟨f, χ|_H⟩_H` for finite groups: induction is adjoint to restriction at the level of characters.
name: Frobenius reciprocity

about: of `L²` of the standard Gaussian — the suitably normalized Hermite polynomials; completeness of the Hermite orthogonal system for the Gaussian weight.
name: The Hermite polynomials are a Hilbert basis

about: the previously announced circle version, extended to arbitrary null-homologous cycles with winding-number weights.
name: The argument principle for a null-homologous cycle

about: , for all derivatives — extending the disc version Mathlib carries to the homology form.
name: Cauchy's integral formula for a null-homologous cycle

about: aspherical spaces and `K(G,1)`s, with the circle as `K(ℤ,1)` and the torus as `K(ℤⁿ,1)` via their universal covers.
name: Eilenberg–MacLane spaces of type K(G,1)

about: the `A/B/C/D/E/F/G` enumeration with its Cartan matrices, as formal data attached to root systems (the labels and their matrices; the classification theorem is not claimed).
name: Dynkin types

about: the previously announced nonvanishing direction is joined by the localization of zeros: every zero of a locally uniform limit of holomorphic functions is a limit of zeros of the approximants, both halves read off one Rouché estimate (coordinated with the Riemann-mapping work in mathlib4#33505). (TauCeti#1646; the nonvanishing form came from TauCeti#1209)
name: Hurwitz's theorem, both directions

about: the Dirichlet integral of a holomorphic function controls the squared lengths of its circle images, so on every annulus some circle has a quantitatively short image: the classical length–area method, with Wolff's lemma as its short-circle consequence.
name: The length–area inequality and Wolff's lemma

about: a holomorphic self-map of the disc contracts the pseudo-hyperbolic distance, and a single equality forces it to be a biholomorphism of the disc with explicit Möbius inverse; this upgrades the infinitesimal inequality announced earlier to the distance form with its equality case (coordinated with mathlib4#33505).
name: The Schwarz–Pick theorem, with rigidity

about: on a simply connected domain, a germ that continues analytically along every path is the germ of a single holomorphic function on the whole domain; the global corollary of the homotopy form announced earlier.
name: The monodromy theorem, global form

about: the unit disc with the hyperbolic distance is a geodesic metric space, and the geodesic between two points is unique.
name: Geodesics in the Poincaré disc

about: subsets homeomorphic to the circle, and the planar domains they bound: the definitions and basic API; the Jordan curve theorem itself is not claimed.
name: Jordan curves and Jordan domains

about: the quotient of grid diagrams of all sizes by cyclic permutation, commutation, and stabilization: the combinatorial notion of link that grid homology (Ozsváth–Stipsicz–Szabó) computes with, joining the grid-state gradings announced earlier; the comparison with embedded links is a separate later target.
name: Grid links: grid diagrams modulo grid moves

about: the classes of finite groups against which Artin's and Brauer's induction theorems are stated, with the closure properties they are used through; the induction theorems themselves are later targets.
name: Elementary and hyperelementary groups

about: two `K`-algebra homomorphisms from a finite-dimensional central simple algebra into a finite-dimensional simple algebra are conjugate by a unit; in particular every algebra automorphism of a finite-dimensional central simple algebra is inner.
name: The Skolem–Noether theorem

about: a harmonic function on a preconnected open subset of the plane attaining an interior local maximum or minimum is constant there, by globalizing the zero case of the planar Harnack inequality announced earlier.
name: The strong maximum principle for planar harmonic functions

about: the first orthogonality relation for matrix coefficients of a finite-dimensional irreducible unitary representation of a compact group under Haar averaging, with the irreducible characters an orthonormal system in `L²` (the Haar-measure counterpart of Mathlib's finite-group `Representation.char_orthonormal`).
name: Schur orthogonality for compact groups

about: every isometry of the hyperbolic distance on the unit disc is a disc automorphism or the conjugate of one, with the automorphism group parametrised by a rotation and a centre; the geodesics announced in the previous update now sit inside a classified isometry group.
name: The isometries of the Poincaré disc, classified

about: two C₀-semigroups on a Banach space with the same infinitesimal generator are equal.
name: A strongly continuous semigroup is determined by its generator

about: the element `w₀` whose inversion set is the full set of positive roots, with the characterizations that an element with no inversions is the identity and that `w₀` maximizes the inversion count.
name: The longest element of a finite Weyl group

about: counting semistandard Young tableaux by shape and content, with the dominance triangularity (`K_{μμ} = 1`, and `K_{μν} = 0` unless `μ` dominates `ν`) and conjugation of partitions reversing the dominance order.
name: Kostka numbers

about: perfect matchings of the `2k` boundary points of a diagram, counted by `(2k − 1)‼` — the combinatorics indexing the basis of the Brauer algebra, the centralizer of the orthogonal and symplectic actions on tensor powers.
name: Brauer diagrams

about: every modular form for SL₂(ℤ) is a polynomial in the Eisenstein series E₄ and E₆ (Serre, *A Course in Arithmetic*, VII.3); this ports Chris Birkbeck's open upstream draft mathlib4#39258 onto the current Mathlib pin.
name: E₄ and E₆ generate the level-one modular forms

about: on a finite-dimensional Hausdorff real manifold, directional differentiation is a linear equivalence between the tangent space at an interior point and the algebraic point derivations on smooth functions, so the geometric and derivation definitions of the tangent space agree (Lee, *Introduction to Smooth Manifolds*).
name: Tangent vectors are point derivations

about: over a field, M ↦ Spec k[M] is an anti-equivalence from finitely generated commutative groups to the group schemes whose coordinate Hopf algebra is spanned by group-like elements (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, 12.8–12.9). (TauCeti#1816, with the essential image characterized in TauCeti#1709)
name: Diagonalizable group schemes are classified by their characters

about: for a commutative Hopf algebra H over any commutative ring, I ↦ Spec(H/I) is an order isomorphism from the Hopf ideals of H (with reversed inclusion) onto the closed subgroup schemes of Spec H (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, 3.15; Waterhouse, §16).
name: Closed subgroup schemes correspond to Hopf ideals

about: natural actions of the point groups A ↦ Hom(H, A) on the scalar extensions A ⊗ V correspond exactly to H-comodule structures on V, with no finiteness, flatness, or projectivity hypotheses (Milne, *Basic Theory of Affine Group Schemes*, VIII).
name: Representations of an affine group scheme are comodules

about: every Weyl orbit meets the closed dominant chamber in exactly one point, and the stabilizer of a dominant weight is generated by the simple reflections in the walls through it (Humphreys, *Reflection Groups and Coxeter Groups*, Ch. 1).
name: The closed dominant chamber is a strict fundamental domain

about: the extreme points of the convex set of exchangeable probability laws on ℕ → α, for α standard Borel, are exactly the i.i.d. product laws: the extreme-point form of de Finetti–Hewitt–Savage (Kallenberg, *Probabilistic Symmetries*, Ch. 1).
name: The extreme exchangeable laws are the i.i.d. laws

about: evaluation at time one of the invariant one-parameter subgroup generated by a tangent vector, with the scaling, identity, and inverse laws and smoothness of the generated subgroup, for groups modeled on a complete normed space.
name: The exponential map of a Lie group

about: Weyl's construction: a Young symmetrizer acting on a tensor power of the standard representation cuts out a GL n-subrepresentation depending, up to isomorphism, only on the shape, and nonzero exactly when the shape has at most n rows (Fulton–Harris, Lecture 6).
name: Weyl modules for GL n

about: a modular form of weight k for a finite-index subgroup Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) whose q-expansion at ∞ vanishes to order beyond k·[SL₂(ℤ):Γ]/12 is zero, and the space of such forms is finite-dimensional; Mathlib master has the level-one case, and this ports the general case from Chris Birkbeck's open draft mathlib4#39000 (Sturm 1987; Diamond–Shurman).
name: The Sturm bound for finite-index subgroups

about: E₄ and E₆ are algebraically independent, upgrading the generation statement announced yesterday (TauCeti#1878) to an algebra isomorphism M(SL₂(ℤ)) ≅ ℂ[E₄, E₆] (Serre, *A Course in Arithmetic*, VII).
name: The level-one modular forms are ℂ[E₄, E₆]

about: the free module on the double cosets H\Δ/H carries a convolution product making it an associative unital ring, and Shimura's criterion — an anti-involution of Δ preserving H and fixing every double coset — forces it to be commutative, the mechanism behind the commutativity of the classical Hecke algebra via the transpose and elementary divisors (Shimura, Ch. 3, Prop. 3.8). (TauCeti#1937; the convolution ring TauCeti#1933, the double-coset API TauCeti#1879)
name: Shimura's Hecke ring, commutative under an anti-involution

about: the reduction map SL₂(ℤ) → SL₂(ℤ/dℤ) is surjective for every d (Shimura §1.6), the input that realizes every unit of ℤ/N as a lower-right entry in Γ₀(N).
name: Strong approximation for SL₂

about: ⟨Ind_H^G 1, Ind_K^G 1⟩ = #(H\G/K), the trivial-character case of Mackey's intertwining-number formula, proved by Burnside's lemma with no algebraic closure needed (Serre, *Linear Representations of Finite Groups*).
name: The pairing of two permutation characters counts double cosets

about: χ_Sym²(g) = (χ(g)² + χ(g²))/2 and χ_Λ²(g) = (χ(g)² − χ(g²))/2, with division-free doubled forms valid over every field (Fulton–Harris, §2.1).
name: The symmetric- and exterior-square character formulas

about: the scalar action ω_χ of the centre of k[G] given by Schur's lemma, with the class-sum identity ω_χ(K_C)·χ(1) = |C|·χ(g) and the integrality of its values — the standard input to χ(1) ∣ |G| and to the Dixon–Schneider algorithm (Isaacs, Ch. 3).
name: The central character of an irreducible representation

about: for a representation V of a finite group G over any field in which |G| is invertible, ν₂(V) = |G|⁻¹ Σ_g χ(g²) equals dim (Sym²V)ᴳ − dim (Λ²V)ᴳ, with the companion splitting dim (V ⊗ V)ᴳ = dim (Sym²V)ᴳ + dim (Λ²V)ᴳ; the real/complex/quaternionic trichotomy for irreducibles is a later milestone (Isaacs; Etingof).
name: The Frobenius–Schur indicator counts invariants in the two squares

about: Frobenius' divisibility theorem: over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, χ(1) ∣ |G|, since the class-sum relation ωᵪ(K_C)·χ(1) = |C|·χ(g_C) and the algebraic integrality of character values make |G|/χ(1) a rational algebraic integer (Serre; Isaacs).
name: The degree of an irreducible character divides the group order

about: the radical built from maximal left ideals agrees with the one built from maximal right ideals, through the elementwise criterion that every 1 + a·x·b is a unit; semiprimarity passes to the opposite ring and a left-Artinian ring is right Noetherian exactly when it is right Artinian, discharging the three standing `proof_wanted` declarations of Mathlib's `WedderburnArtin.lean` (Lam).
name: The Jacobson radical is left-right symmetric

about: inside a finite-dimensional simple K-algebra A, the centralizer C of a central simple subalgebra B is again simple and dim B · dim C = dim A, through the identification C ≅ End of A over B ⊗ Aᵐᵒᵖ (Gille–Szamuely; Knapp).
name: The centralizer theorem for central simple algebras

about: the Dirichlet series Σ aₙ n⁻ˢ of the announced modular-form L-function (TauCeti#1917) extends to an entire function for a cusp form of positive weight at arithmetic level: TauCeti#1987 rebuilt the interface on Mathlib's `ModularForm.L`, and the identity theorem transfers Mathlib's continuation (`CuspForm.differentiable_L`) across the half-plane identification — completing the milestone that bullet left open (Diamond–Shurman).
name: The cusp-form L-series is entire

about: for a finite-dimensional smooth real Lie group, the exponential of TauCeti#1801 is C^∞ on the whole Lie algebra — Picard–Lindelöf parameter dependence gives smoothness near zero and exp(m·v) = (exp v)^m globalises it — with derivative at zero the identity (TauCeti#2005) (Hall; Duistermaat–Kolk).
name: The Lie-group exponential is smooth

about: on the unit group Rˣ of a finite-dimensional real normed algebra, the abstract Lie-group exponential recovers exp(x) = Σ xⁿ/n! under the canonical identification Lie(Rˣ) ≅ R, and specialises on GL(n, ℝ) to the matrix exponential with its diagonal, transpose, and conjugation formulas (TauCeti#1902) (Hall; Bourbaki LIE III).
name: The abstract and Banach-algebra exponentials coincide

about: for f, g meromorphic on an open set U and a closed piecewise-C¹ cycle γ null-homologous in U with ‖f − g‖ < ‖f‖ + ‖g‖ on γ, the winding-weighted counts of zeros minus poles of f and g agree, extending the disc form of TauCeti#1179 off the circle in the symmetric two-sided phrasing (Conway).
name: Rouché's theorem for a null-homologous cycle

about: every geodesic line of the disc (classified in TauCeti#1512) traces a Euclidean diameter or 𝔻 ∩ ∂B(c, R) with ‖c‖² = R² + 1, the Pythagorean form of orthogonality to the boundary circle (Anderson).
name: Poincaré geodesics are Euclidean circles orthogonal to the unit circle

about: the integral matrices of positive determinant lie in the commensurator of SL_n(ℤ) (Shimura's Lemma 3.10), founding the integral Hecke ring of GL_n on Mathlib's Hecke-triple class — the concrete arithmetic instance behind the announced Hecke-ring layer (Shimura §3.2).
name: The arithmetic Hecke triple for GL_n

about: the (ℤ/N)ˣ-action ⟨d⟩ on modular forms of level Γ₁(N), built through the Γ₀(N)/Γ₁(N) quotient on the strong-approximation input of TauCeti#1882, with membership in the χ-space the classical nebentypus relation f∣[k]γ = χ(d_γ)·f and the parity lemma — χ(−1) = (−1)^k on any nonzero space — in TauCeti#2013; ports the AINTLIB LeanModularForms development (Diamond–Shurman).
name: Diamond operators and the nebentypus character spaces

about: the triangular interlacing integer arrays indexing the Gelfand–Tsetlin basis of an irreducible rational GL_n-representation, with the top row a dominant weight as a theorem, the top-row-deletion bijection realising the branching recursion, and finiteness of the patterns over a fixed top row (Gelfand–Tsetlin; Molev).
name: Gelfand–Tsetlin patterns

about: over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, a finite-dimensional irreducible module over a Lie algebra generated by an sl₂ triple has a unique highest weight n ∈ ℕ and is the standard module V(n) of dimension n + 1, and every submodule of a finite-dimensional module has a complement (TauCeti#2099), so every such module is ⨁ V(nᵢ); built on Mathlib's sl₂-triple and primitive-vector API, with V(n) constructed in TauCeti#2015 (Humphreys §7; Fulton–Harris).
name: The irreducible sl₂-modules, and complete reducibility

about: two decompositions of a module of finite length into indecomposable summands are matched by a bijection of their index sets under which corresponding summands are isomorphic, in Azumaya's generality where one family need only have local endomorphism rings; the existence half and Fitting's lemma (TauCeti#1460) were already here, and this is the uniqueness they were missing (Lam; Anderson–Fuller).
name: The Krull–Schmidt theorem

about: over an algebraically closed field in which |G| is invertible the irreducible characters are exactly as many as G has conjugacy classes and none is missing (TauCeti#2031), so they assemble into a square matrix carrying both orthogonality relations — orthonormal rows, and columns orthogonal weighted by class size — whose degree column consists of positive integers dividing |G| whose squares sum to |G| (Serre; Isaacs).
name: The character table of a finite group

about: for a finite-dimensional smooth Lie group, X ↦ (t ↦ exp(tX)) is a bijection from the Lie algebra onto the continuous homomorphisms ℝ → G, so such a subgroup has a unique generator and is automatically smooth — the structural statement behind the exponential map of TauCeti#1801, shown smooth in TauCeti#1892 (Hall; Lee).
name: Continuous one-parameter subgroups are the exponentials

about: the pairing ⟨f, g⟩ = ∫_D conj(f)·g·y^k dμ of modular forms over a fundamental domain, Hermitian and positive definite, with the integrand of a cusp form against a modular form integrable over the standard domain 𝒟; built on Mathlib's pointwise Petersson function and invariant measure, and ported from the AINTLIB LeanModularForms development (Miyake; Iwaniec).
name: The Petersson inner product

about: for an additive Haar measure on an n-dimensional real normed space, the centred maximal function Mf satisfies the weak-type (1,1) bound t·μ{x : Mf x > t} ≤ 4ⁿ ∫ ‖f‖, proved from Mathlib's Vitali covering lemmas; the first item of the harmonic-analysis lane the PDE roadmap builds on (Stein, *Singular Integrals* Ch. I).
name: The Hardy–Littlewood maximal inequality

about: every submodule U of the Young permutation module M^μ satisfies S^μ ≤ U or U ≤ (S^μ)^⊥ for the tabloid form, and since that form is positive definite the two meet only at zero, so the Specht module — constructed from polytabloids in TauCeti#1984 — is irreducible over ℚ, giving the classical model of the irreducible representations of the symmetric group (James, LNM 682).
name: James's submodule theorem

about: the diamond-operator character spaces announced in TauCeti#1959 are now shown to span M_k(Γ₁(N)) and to be independent, so M_k(Γ₁(N)) = ⨁_χ M_k(N, χ) as an internal direct sum, with the cusp-form analogue and a version relative to any diamond-invariant subspace (Diamond–Shurman §5.2).
name: The nebentypus decomposition of M_k(Γ₁(N))

about: the Schur polynomial of a partition in a finite alphabet, defined as the generating function of the semistandard Young tableaux of that shape weighted by content, with its coefficients identified as the Kostka numbers of TauCeti#1684 (Macdonald I.5; Stanley EC2 Ch. 7).
name: Schur polynomials as tableau generating functions

about: for H ≤ G finite and A a finite-dimensional representation of H over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, Ind_H^G A is irreducible exactly when A is irreducible and, for every double coset HsH other than H itself, the restrictions of A and of its conjugate ˢA to H ∩ sHs⁻¹ share no nonzero intertwiner (Serre §7.4).
name: The Mackey irreducibility criterion

about: the diagonal p₀ = 1, p₁ = ∞ case of Marcinkiewicz interpolation, applied to upgrade the weak-type (1,1) bound of TauCeti#2095 to ‖Mf‖_p ≤ C_p‖f‖_p for every 1 < p < ∞, the classical strong maximal theorem (Grafakos, *Classical Fourier Analysis* §1.3.1, §2.1.1).
name: Marcinkiewicz interpolation, and the strong (p,p) maximal inequality

about: over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, the indicator of an irreducible representation is 1 exactly when it carries a nonzero invariant symmetric form, −1 exactly when it carries a nonzero invariant alternating form, and 0 exactly when it carries no nonzero invariant bilinear form — the orthogonal/symplectic/complex classification, and the milestone the indicator bullet of TauCeti#2011 left open (Serre §13.2; Isaacs Ch. 4).
name: The Frobenius–Schur trichotomy

about: each vector regular for a base lies in the open chamber of exactly one Weyl-group translate of the base, so the closed dominant chamber is a fundamental domain and the action on chambers is simply transitive (Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras*, §10).
name: The Weyl group acts simply transitively on the Weyl chambers

about: `Spv A`, the equivalence classes of valuations on `A` with the topology generated by the rational inequalities, ported from Chris Birkbeck's open upstream draft mathlib4#38009 as the opening target of the adic-spaces roadmap; landing alongside it are the two inputs toward its spectrality, the patch criterion of Wedhorn Proposition 3.31 (spectralSpace_of_isClopen_generateFrom, TauCeti#2278) and the calculus of pro-constructible subsets with the spectrality of their subspaces (TauCeti#2289, TauCeti#2290) — the spectrality of `Spv A` itself is the next milestone, not yet concluded.
name: The valuation spectrum of a ring

about: `Spv A` is spectral, assembled from the patch presentation of the space and the patch criterion for spectral spaces; this is the milestone the `Spv` bullet of TauCeti#2262 named as outstanding, now closed (Wedhorn, *Adic Spaces*, Theorem 4.9, from Propositions 4.7 and 3.31).
name: The valuation spectrum is a spectral space

about: a function continuous on [0,∞) and completely monotone on (0,∞) is the Laplace transform of a **unique** finite positive measure on ℝ≥0; both directions were announced with TauCeti#1482, and what is new is uniqueness of the representing measure, which turns the correspondence into a bijection (Widder, *The Laplace Transform* Ch. IV).
name: The Hausdorff–Bernstein–Widder theorem

about: setting the last variable to 1 expands a Schur polynomial as the sum of the Schur polynomials of the shapes interlacing it, the restriction rule from GL_n to GL_{n−1} in symmetric-function form, complementing the tableau definition of TauCeti#2156 (Fulton, *Young Tableaux* §2.2; Macdonald I.5 Ex. 3).
name: The branching rule for Schur polynomials

about: every affine group scheme of finite type over a field admits a faithful finite-dimensional representation, a closed immersion into GLₙ, built from finite coefficient-generating comodules (Waterhouse §3.4). (TauCeti#2582, with TauCeti#2386, TauCeti#2457)
name: The embedding theorem for affine group schemes

about: over ℚ the Specht module of every partition of n is an irreducible representation of Sₙ, and two are isomorphic only when the partitions agree — one irreducible per partition, via James's dominance lemma (James §4). (TauCeti#2091, TauCeti#2446, with TauCeti#2245)
name: The Specht modules, irreducible and pairwise distinct

about: a finite-dimensional module over a Lie algebra generated by an sl₂ triple, in characteristic zero over an algebraically closed field, is an internal direct sum of finitely many irreducibles, each a standard irreducible of sl₂ (Humphreys §7).
name: Complete reducibility and classification for sl₂

about: `BrauerGroup K` carries its commutative group structure, multiplication induced by ⊗ and inverse the opposite algebra, supplying the structure upstream Mathlib's `BrauerGroup/Defs.lean` records as its first TODO (Gille–Szamuely §2).
name: The Brauer group is a group

about: over any field, an elliptic curve with j-invariant away from 0 and 1728 has automorphism group {±1}, uniformly in the characteristic (Silverman III.10).
name: The automorphism group of an elliptic curve with j ∉ {0, 1728}

about: an explicit model over any commutative ring with the transformation laws b₂ ↦ Db₂, c₄ ↦ D²c₄, c₆ ↦ D³c₆, Δ ↦ D⁶Δ for D = t² − 4n, elliptic whenever D is a unit; with the twist by a quadratic extension and, behind it, Galois descent for changes of variables and affine points (TauCeti#2268).
name: The quadratic twist of a Weierstrass curve

about: the character of Res_K Ind_H^G A is the sum over double cosets KsH of the characters of the Mackey summands Ind over K ⊓ sHs⁻¹, with the intertwining-number formula for dim Hom of two induced representations as its pairing form (Serre §7.3–7.4).
name: The Mackey decomposition formula

about: the class of a normalized 2-cocycle in Mathlib's `groupCohomology.H2`, equal for two factor sets exactly when they differ by a coboundary; with projective representations and their factor sets identified with modules over the twisted group algebra (TauCeti#2016).
name: H² classifies factor sets

about: in Friedrichs form: a C¹ function supported in {a ≤ xᵢ ≤ b} satisfies ‖u‖_p ≤ (b−a)‖Du‖_p for 1 ≤ p < ∞, and no inequality of this shape holds on the whole space (Gilbarg–Trudinger §7.8).
name: The Poincaré inequality on a slab

about: every integer matrix of determinant one is a product of elementary transvections; with Smith normal form over ℤ by determinant-one operations — positive diagonal, divisibility chain, unique (TauCeti#2048).
name: SL_n(ℤ) is generated by transvections

about: the ramification locus of a module-finite torsion-free extension with separable fraction-field extension is finite, complementing Mathlib's openness of the unramified locus (Neukirch III.2).
name: A separable extension of Dedekind domains ramifies at only finitely many primes

about: on the announced GL_n foundation, the classical computation layer: the divisor-pair basis with T(n), deg T(n) = σ₁(n), and the recurrence T(p^{r+2}) = T(p)·T(p^{r+1}) − p·⟨p⟩·T(p^r) making the local Hecke algebra polynomial in T(p) (Shimura Thm 3.24).
name: The GL(2) Hecke operators T(n)

about: two plans sharing an intermediate marginal admit a joint law on X × Y × Z with the given (X,Y)- and (Y,Z)-marginals, the composition step transport theory runs on (Villani, *Optimal Transport* Ch. 1).
name: The gluing lemma for transport plans

about: the foundations of Huber's theory for the adic-spaces roadmap: bounded and power-bounded elements, rings of integral elements and Huber pairs, restricted power series A⟨T₁,…,Tₖ⟩ with the strongly noetherian condition, A° integrally closed, completions stay Huber/Tate, and the separating examples — ℤ_p is Huber but not Tate, ℚ_p and K⸨X⸩ are Tate (Wedhorn §5–6).
name: Huber rings, Tate rings, and Huber pairs

about: for a compact Hausdorff group, the normalized matrix coefficients of a skeleton of the unitary dual — constructed, not assumed — form a Hilbert basis of `L²(G)`, and the representative ring they span is uniformly dense in `C(G)` (Peter–Weyl, *Math. Ann.* 97, 1927).
name: The Peter–Weyl theorem

about: over any field of characteristic ≠ 2, the orthogonal group of a finite-dimensional nondegenerate quadratic space is generated by its reflections in vectors of invertible norm, the input for Pin surjectivity; Mathlib carries the real inner-product case with the reflection-count bound (Lawson–Michelsohn, *Spin Geometry*, I §2).
name: The Cartan–Dieudonné theorem, generation form

about: the exact sequence relating `Hⁿ(U ⊔ V, M)` to `Hⁿ(U, M) ⊕ Hⁿ(V, M)` and `Hⁿ(U ⊓ V, M)` with its connecting map, together with its vanishing consequences (Stacks Project, *Cohomology of Sheaves*, Mayer–Vietoris).
name: Mayer–Vietoris for the cohomology of sheaves of modules on a scheme

about: an operator on a real Banach space generates a strongly continuous contraction semigroup exactly when it is densely defined and m-dissipative (Engel–Nagel, Theorem II.3.15; Pazy, Theorem 1.4.3).
name: The Lumer–Phillips generation theorem

about: `Matᵢ(D) ≃ Mat_κ(E)` exactly when `ι ≃ κ` and `D ≃ E`, so the degree and the division ring of a matrix presentation of a simple Artinian ring are invariants, completing the existence statement announced earlier (Lam, *A First Course in Noncommutative Rings*, Ch. 1).
name: The uniqueness clause of Wedderburn–Artin

about: for a meromorphic weight-`k` level-one form, `Σ_q ord_q + ½·ord_i + ⅓·ord_ρ + ord_∞ = k/12`, with zeros and poles allowed at the elliptic corners `i` and `ρ`; ports Chris Birkbeck's LeanModularForms valence-formula development onto the current pin (Serre, *A Course in Arithmetic*, VII §3).
name: The valence formula

about: `μ ↦ S^μ` is a bijection from the partitions of `n` onto the isomorphism classes of simple `ℚ[Sₙ]`-modules, upgrading the irreducibility and pairwise distinctness announced earlier to the full classification (James, *The Representation Theory of the Symmetric Groups*, Ch. 4).
name: The Specht modules classify the irreducible rational representations of Sₙ

about: two root systems carrying bases of the same Cartan type are isomorphic as root pairings, the rigidity half of the Cartan–Killing classification (Bourbaki, *Lie Groups and Lie Algebras*, VI §4).
name: Root systems of the same Dynkin type are isomorphic

about: in characteristic zero, every nonzero finite-dimensional module over a Killing-semisimple Lie algebra has a highest weight vector whose weight is dominant integral, and irreducible modules are highest weight modules (Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*, §20).
name: Existence of highest weight vectors

about: for a Dedekind domain, `Cl(𝒪_S)` is `Cl(R)` modulo the classes of the primes in `S`, hence finite whenever `Cl(R)` is, and for finite `S` the `S`-units are finitely generated whenever `Rˣ` is — the two finiteness inputs of weak Mordell–Weil (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, I §11).
name: The class group and unit group of the S-integers

about: every symplectic form on a finite-dimensional real vector space is compatible with some almost complex structure, the nonemptiness half of the standard statement, with contractibility not addressed (McDuff–Salamon, *J-holomorphic Curves and Symplectic Topology*, §2.2).
name: Every symplectic vector space carries a compatible almost complex structure

about: the tangent Lie algebra of the algebraic group SLₙ is Mathlib's classical `sl n`, over every commutative coefficient algebra (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, §10).
name: The Lie algebra of SLₙ is the trace-zero matrices

about: a surjective equivariant additive map from a complete first-countable nonarchimedean group onto a Baire space is open when the scalars carry a zero sequence of units, the open-mapping input for Wedhorn's Proposition 6.16 (Henkel, arXiv:1407.5647).
name: Henkel's open mapping theorem

about: the `p`-local Hecke ring of GLₙ is the polynomial ring `ℤ[X₁, …, Xₙ]` on the diagonal prime double cosets, proved in the two cases the classical theory uses; ports the AINTLIB development (Shimura, *Introduction to the Arithmetic Theory of Automorphic Functions*, Theorem 3.20).
name: Shimura's Theorem 3.20 for GL₁ and GL₂

about: the restricted power series of a Huber ring with power-boundedness weights `T`, now complete with its topology, functoriality, density of polynomials, and the universal property for power-bounded weighted variables (Wedhorn, *Adic Spaces*, 5.49–5.50).
name: Wedhorn's weighted restricted power series `A⟨X⟩_T`

about: a function on a finite-dimensional real inner-product space is continuous with positive-definite subtraction kernel exactly when it is the Fourier transform of a unique finite positive measure (Bochner 1932; Rudin, *Fourier Analysis on Groups*, Theorem 1.4.3).
name: Bochner's theorem

about: for `N ◁ G`, the irreducible `N`-constituents of the restriction of an irreducible representation of `G` form a single `G`-orbit, and `G` permutes the isotypic components transitively; the inertia-group induction clause is a later milestone (Isaacs, *Character Theory of Finite Groups*, Theorem 6.2).
name: Clifford's theorem, single-orbit form

about: a length-decreasing reflection deletes one letter from any word for a Weyl-group element, with the deletion condition and the subword property as corollaries, toward the Coxeter presentation of the Weyl group (Humphreys, *Reflection Groups and Coxeter Groups*, §5.8).
name: The strong exchange condition

about: for `j(E) ∉ {0, 1728}`, a curve isomorphic to `E` over `L` is isomorphic over `K` to `E` or to its quadratic twist by `L`, and the two are distinct — the order-two `H¹(Gal(L/K), Aut E)` made explicit, upgrading the twist construction announced earlier (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, X.5.4).
name: The forms of an elliptic curve split by a quadratic extension

about: `#{g : g² = x} = Σ_χ ν₂(χ)·χ(x)` over the irreducible characters, upgrading the previously announced indicator to the square-root counting formula it exists for (Isaacs, Ch. 4).
name: The Frobenius–Schur involution count

about: `e_χ = (deg χ/|G|)·Σ_g χ(g⁻¹)·g` for each irreducible character, pairwise orthogonal and summing to `1`: the dictionary between the character table and the Wedderburn decomposition (Webb, *A Course in Finite Group Representation Theory*, §3.6).
name: The primitive central idempotents of a group algebra

about: the subspace of valuations with `cΓ_v(I) = Γ_v` is spectral for any ideal `I` sharing its radical with a finitely generated one, extending the previously announced spectrality of `Spv A` to the subspace Wedhorn's retraction `r_I` runs on (Wedhorn, *Adic Spaces*, Lemma 7.5).
name: Spv (A, I) is a spectral space

about: the distributional derivative against compactly supported smooth test functions, with almost-everywhere uniqueness and agreement with the classical derivative: the opening of the Sobolev development (Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, §5.2).
name: Weak derivatives on an open set

about: the split Cayley algebra over an arbitrary commutative ring, built as Zorn vector matrices: an 8-dimensional alternative composition algebra whose norm N⟨a, b, v, w⟩ = ab − v⬝w is multiplicative, with the rank-two equation, the flexible law and the three Moufang identities (Springer–Veldkamp, *Octonions, Jordan Algebras and Exceptional Groups*).
name: The split octonions

about: an affine group scheme over a field is recovered from its representations: the algebra-valued points of a commutative Hopf algebra correspond multiplicatively to the tensor automorphisms of the fibre functor on finite comodules (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, §9.4).
name: Tannakian reconstruction

about: over a perfect field a point of an affine algebraic group is the commuting product of a semisimple and a unipotent point of the same group, acting on every finite-dimensional representation by the linear Jordan factors; this is the group-scheme form of the endomorphism-level decomposition announced earlier, reconstructed through the Tannakian equivalence above (Springer, *Linear Algebraic Groups*, §2.4).
name: The Jordan decomposition of an algebraic group element

about: over a finite field with q elements the q-power map on the coordinate ring of a Weierstrass curve is an isogeny π_q of the curve with itself, of degree q (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, II.2.11).
name: The Frobenius isogeny

about: a finite-dimensional central division algebra D over K contains a subfield of degree exactly deg D, the square root of dim_K D, and that subfield splits D (Gille–Szamuely, *Central Simple Algebras and Galois Cohomology*).
name: Maximal subfields of a central division algebra

about: over any commutative ring U(𝔤) carries the comultiplication making every Lie generator primitive, together with its counit and the antipode x ↦ −x, which reverses products and is involutive (Bourbaki, *Lie Groups and Lie Algebras*, Ch. I).
name: The universal enveloping algebra is a cocommutative Hopf algebra

about: the class in H²(G, kˣ) of the factor set of a projective representation depends only on the projective action and vanishes exactly when the representation is an ordinary linear one rescaled by units, and every class arises this way (Karpilovsky, *Projective Representations of Finite Groups*).
name: The Schur multiplier as the obstruction to linearising a projective representation

about: the generalized winding number of a closed piecewise-C¹ immersion γ about s is still (1/2π)∫(x ẏ − y ẋ)/(x² + y²) dt when γ passes through s, provided the crossings are interior and C^{1,1} on each side, with boundedness and integrability of the integrand derived rather than assumed; the off-curve case was announced earlier (Hungerbühler–Wasem, arXiv:1808.00997, Prop. 2.3).
name: The Hungerbühler–Wasem bounded-integrand formula

about: differentiating conjugation on a Lie group at the identity in the direction X carries a left-invariant field Y to ⁅X, Y⁆ (Knapp, *Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction*, Ch. I).
name: The differential of Ad is ad

about: for a module generated by a highest weight vector v of weight λ over a Killing-semisimple Lie algebra, with no finite-dimensionality assumed, every weight χ satisfies λ − χ ∈ Q⁺, the cone of nonnegative integer combinations of the simple roots, and the λ-weight space is the line K·v, so λ and v are pinned down up to a scalar (Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*, §20).
name: The weights of a highest weight module

about: a comodule over the monoid algebra R[G] is the internal direct sum of its weight submodules, on each of which a point of D(G) = Spec R[G] acts through the character g (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, Thm 12.12; Waterhouse §3.2).
name: Representations of a diagonalizable group are diagonalizable

about: the first-order Sobolev space on an open subset of a Euclidean space, cut out of the Lᵖ value-gradient jets by the distributional integration-by-parts identity and proved complete for every 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞, with membership shown to be exactly weak differentiability with the recorded gradient (Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, §5.2).
name: The weak Sobolev space W^{1,p}(Ω)

about: for a polarization V = W ⊕ W' ⊕ L of a quadratic space, the exterior algebra ⋀·W is made a module over the Clifford algebra of Q, with exterior multiplication as creation, contraction against the polarization pairing as annihilation and the grade involution on the remainder; stated over an arbitrary commutative ring (Chevalley, *The Algebraic Theory of Spinors*).
name: The spinor representation in its Fock model

about: the continuous valuations on A bounded by 1 on the subring A⁺, as a subset of the valuation spectrum, with its membership criterion and antitonicity in A⁺; the point set only, with spectrality and the structure presheaf to follow, and also being formalised in mathlib4#42315, which instead bundles a chosen representative (Wedhorn, *Adic Spaces*, Def. 7.23).
name: The adic spectrum Spa(A, A⁺)

about: the annihilation and creation operators a = (x + d/dx)/√2 and a† = (x − d/dx)/√2 are continuous linear operators on the real Schwartz space 𝒮(ℝ, ℝ) with aa† − a†a = id, they ladder the Hermite functions by a ψₙ = √n ψₙ₋₁ and a† ψₙ = √(n+1) ψₙ₊₁, and the number operator N = a†a and the harmonic oscillator H = N + ½ have the ψₙ as eigenvectors with eigenvalues n and n + ½; the extension to unbounded operators on L²(ℝ) is a later milestone (Hall, *Quantum Theory for Mathematicians*).
name: The canonical commutation relation on Schwartz space

about: for a conditionally i.i.d. process with directing measure ν and a bounded measurable observable f, the averages (1/n)Σ_{i<n} f(Xᵢ) converge almost surely to ∫ f dν, so for an exchangeable process on a standard Borel state space the empirical frequency of each fixed measurable set converges almost surely to the mass ν gives it; the weak convergence of the empirical measures themselves needs a topology on the state space and is a separate later milestone (Kallenberg, *Probabilistic Symmetries and Invariance Principles*, §1.1).
name: The conditional strong law of large numbers

about: for a nonzero weight-k level-one form, Σ_q ord_q f + ½·ord_i f + ⅓·ord_ρ f + ord_∞ f = k/12, the sum running over the non-elliptic SL₂(ℤ)-orbits and the only hypothesis being f ≠ 0; the form announced on 11 August was the intermediate one, quantified over a finite divisor set with two capture hypotheses and summed over three explicit boundary families, and this is the textbook orbit-sum statement those were bookkeeping for (Serre, *A Course in Arithmetic*, VII §3).
name: The valence formula

about: Chevalley's τ = exp(ad e)∘exp(ad(−f))∘exp(ad e) attached to an sl₂ triple negates and swaps the triple, fixes the joint centraliser of e and f, acts on a Cartan subalgebra as the coreflection y ↦ y − α(y)α^∨, and carries the root space L_β onto L_{β − β(α^∨)α}, so every reflection of the root system of a split Killing Lie algebra comes from an automorphism of the algebra (Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*, Proposition 14.3).
name: Every reflection of a root system is realised by an automorphism of the Lie algebra

about: Spa(A, A⁺) is spectral for every Huber ring A and subring A⁺, exhibited as a pro-constructible subspace of Spv(A, IA); the point set went out on 13 August with spectrality named as still to come, and this is that step, reached through Wedhorn's Theorem 7.10, which identifies Cont A inside Spv(A, IA), and Corollary 7.12, which makes Cont A itself spectral; the space is also being formalised in mathlib4#42315 (Wedhorn, *Adic Spaces*, Theorem 7.35).
name: The adic spectrum is a spectral space

about: in any associative ℚ-algebra whose elements E, F, H satisfy the sl₂ relations, E⁽ᵐ⁾ F⁽ⁿ⁾ = Σ_{k ≤ min(m,n)} F⁽ⁿ⁻ᵏ⁾ · (H − m − n + 2k choose k) · E⁽ᵐ⁻ᵏ⁾, with generalized binomial coefficients and no denominators — the normal-ordering rule that makes the Kostant ℤ-form of a universal enveloping algebra closed under multiplication (Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*, §26.2).
name: Kostant's rank-one straightening formula

about: for a multilinear map f of a finite family of arguments, Σ_{S ⊆ ι} (−1)^|S| f(Σ_{i ∉ S} mᵢ, …, Σ_{i ∉ S} mᵢ) = Σ_σ f(m_{σ(1)}, …, m_{σ(n)}) with no invertibility assumed, so the diagonal values of f already determine every symmetrization; over a ring in which (#ι)! is invertible this identifies the symmetric tensors of ⨂ M with the span of the pure powers ⨂ᵢ x (Fulton–Harris, *Representation Theory: A First Course*, Appendix B.1).
name: Polarization for multilinear maps

about: the character of Symᵈ(ℂ²) on the maximal torus is χ_d(θ) = sin((d+1)θ)/sin θ off the multiples of π, where it is (d+1)cosᵈθ, together with the unconditional telescoped form sin θ · χ_d = sin((d+1)θ) that holds everywhere; this is the rank-one case, the general Weyl character formula being a later milestone (Bröcker–tom Dieck, *Representations of Compact Lie Groups*, II §5).
name: The Weyl character formula for SU(2)

about: the function-field extension an isogeny of Weierstrass curves measures is finite, the inseparable case included, so deg φ is a genuine positive integer, it is 1 exactly when the function-field pullback is onto, and deg(ψ ∘ φ) = deg ψ · deg φ (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, II.2).
name: The degree of an isogeny is finite, positive and multiplicative

about: ∫₀^R sin(ax)/x dx → π/2 for every a > 0, evaluated along a contour that passes through the pole using the Hungerbühler–Wasem on-contour residue theorem.
name: The Dirichlet integral

about: `normEDS b c d` satisfies the four-index elliptic relation over any commutative ring with no hypothesis on the parameters, giving the elliptic half of the `IsEllipticDvdSequence` TODO recorded in Mathlib's own EDS file.
name: A normalised EDS is an elliptic net

about: the image of the set where every derivative of order 1 to k vanishes is null; this is the higher-regularity dimension range, alongside the equal-dimension and dimension-increasing cases announced earlier.
name: Sard's lemma on the flat stratum

about: the ℤ-valued character of each Specht module and the resulting table indexed by partitions; the earlier announcement was the character table of a general finite group, this is the concrete symmetric-group one together with integrality of the characters.
name: The character table of Sₙ

about: Lyapunov–Schmidt reduction: in suitable local coordinates a Fredholm map is a linear surjection paired with an obstruction map valued in a finite-dimensional space.
name: The local normal form of a Fredholm map

about: Diaconis–Freedman: a finitely exchangeable law is the law of a sample drawn at uniformly chosen distinct indices from a random finite population.
name: Finite exchangeability as sampling without replacement

about: 4 at i, 6 at ρ and 2 at every other point of ℍ, established at every point rather than only inside the standard fundamental domain.
name: Orders of the point stabilisers of the modular group

about: the pinned root datum, whose 240 roots come from a completeness proof for the norm-two vectors of the E₈ lattice rather than a tabulated reflection action.
name: The simply connected root datum of type E₈

about: Quillen exact structures on an additive category, built on kernel–cokernel pairs, in Bühler's axiomatisation.
name: Exact structures

about: every nonempty connected finite-type Cartan matrix is, after a simultaneous relabelling of rows and columns, the standard Cartan matrix of exactly one valid Dynkin type Aₙ, Bₙ, Cₙ, Dₙ, E₆, E₇, E₈, F₄, G₂, and hence every irreducible reduced crystallographic finite root system has a unique Dynkin type; together with the rigidity statement announced earlier (TauCeti#2532) this closes the classification the "Dynkin types" bullet (TauCeti#1431) explicitly left open (Bourbaki, *Lie Groups and Lie Algebras*, VI §4; Humphreys §11).
name: The Cartan–Killing classification of finite-type Cartan matrices

about: on a finite-dimensional real Lie group, (exp(tX/n)·exp(tY/n))ⁿ → exp(t(X+Y)) as n → ∞ for left-invariant derivations X, Y, proved from a general power-limit lemma for curves whose local logarithm has prescribed derivative; this is the addition-closure input for the Lie algebra of a closed subgroup, with Cartan's closed-subgroup theorem itself a later milestone.
name: The Lie–Trotter product formula

about: for a finite-dimensional module M over a Killing-semisimple Lie algebra over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, dim M_{w·χ} = dim M_χ for every element w of the Weyl group, so the set of weights is Weyl-stable; proved directly from the rank-one sl₂ theory along root strings rather than through Weyl's complete reducibility theorem (Humphreys §21.2).
name: Weyl-group invariance of weight multiplicities

about: over any field F, two non-scalar elements of GL₂(F) are conjugate exactly when they share trace and determinant (rational canonical form in size two), so the classes are indexed by Fˣ ⊔ (F × Fˣ), and GL₂(𝔽_q) has exactly q² − 1 conjugacy classes, the number of its irreducible complex characters (Bonnafé, *Representations of SL₂(𝔽_q)*, ch. 1).
name: The conjugacy classes of GL₂ over a field

about: every finite-dimensional comodule over the monoid-algebra coalgebra k[G] of a commutative monoid over a field is completely reducible, so every diagonalizable group D(G) — split tori included — is linearly reductive over every field, with no finite-generation or connectedness hypothesis (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, Thm 12.12; Waterhouse §3.2).
name: Diagonalizable groups are linearly reductive

about: `normEDS b c d k · complEDS b c d k n = normEDS b c d (n·k)` over any commutative ring with no hypothesis on b, c, d, so W(k) ∣ W(nk) for every k, n; with the elliptic-net half announced earlier (TauCeti#3270) this discharges both conjuncts of the `IsEllipticDvdSequence` TODO recorded in Mathlib's own EDS file.
name: A normalised EDS is a divisibility sequence

about: finite dualization is an anti-equivalence of the category of finite locally free bicommutative Hopf algebras over any commutative ring, extending the field case announced earlier (TauCeti#3290); the field case is separately transported through Spec to an anti-equivalence of finite commutative affine group schemes over a field (TauCeti#3307).
name: Cartier duality over a general base

about: a submodule N ≤ P is superfluous when N ⊔ K = ⊤ forces K = ⊤, and a projective cover of M is a surjection P → M from a projective module with superfluous kernel; uniqueness up to an isomorphism commuting with the covering maps is proved, superfluous submodules are identified with the submodules of the Jacobson radical when the submodule lattice is coatomic, and existence over semiperfect rings is left for later (Anderson–Fuller, *Rings and Categories of Modules*, §17).
name: Projective covers and superfluous submodules

about: for a polarization V = W ⊕ W' of a quadratic space with no line summand, the exterior parity splitting ⋀W = ⋀ᵉᵛᵉⁿW ⊕ ⋀ᵒᵈᵈW of the spinor module is a splitting of the spin representation into two subrepresentations S⁺, S⁻, because the spin group lies in the even Clifford algebra and Clifford elements of parity i shift exterior parity by i; stated over any commutative ring, with irreducibility and dimensions of the summands not proved (Fulton–Harris §20.1).
name: The half-spin representations

about: a densely defined operator A on a real Banach space whose resolvent powers satisfy ‖R(λ, A)ⁿ‖ ≤ M/(λ − ω)ⁿ generates a strongly continuous semigroup whose generator is exactly A, with growth bound (ω, M) (Engel–Nagel, *One-Parameter Semigroups for Linear Evolution Equations*, Thm II.3.8); the uniqueness direction was announced earlier, and this closes the milestone.
name: The Hille–Yosida generation theorem

about: for m ≤ n, the m-coordinate marginal of an n-exchangeable process differs from the mixture of m-fold products of the empirical distribution of its n-population by at most m(m − 1)/2n, on every measurable event and in both directions (Diaconis–Freedman, *Finite exchangeable sequences*, Ann. Probab. 8 (1980)); the infinite de Finetti–Ryll-Nardzewski theorem was announced earlier.
name: The finite de Finetti approximation

about: Symᵈ(ℂ²) is irreducible for every d, and two are equivalent exactly when their degrees agree, so they are pairwise inequivalent; the maximal torus alone cannot see this, and the argument turns on a single rational rotation in SU(2) with no vanishing entry. Exhaustion — that every finite-dimensional irreducible of SU(2) is one of these — is the remaining half of the classification.
name: The symmetric powers of the standard representation of SU(2) are irreducible

about: the "dog on a leash" lemma: closed curves with dist(γ₁ t, γ₀ t) < dist(γ₀ t, w) at every parameter have the same winding number about w. For piecewise-C¹ curves this yields invariance along the straight-line homotopy from the geometric hypothesis w ∉ [γ₀ t, γ₁ t] alone, with no regularity asked of the homotopy, where the form already available needed one that was C² on the square (Ahlfors, *Complex Analysis*, Ch. 4).
name: Proximity invariance of the winding number

about: for integral divided-power exponentials, E_x(t) E_y(u) = E_y(u) E_z(tu) E_w(t²u) E_v(t³u) E_s(t³u²) E_x(t): the case where the roots iα + jβ with i, j > 0 are α + β, 2α + β, 3α + β and 3α + 2β. No factorial is inverted, so it holds in arbitrary characteristic (Carter, *Simple Groups of Lie Type*, Thm 5.2.2). The chain β, α + β, 2α + β for types B, C and F₄ is TauCeti#3513; the remaining G₂ pair α, α + β and the transport to the Kostant root subgroups are not done here.
name: The Chevalley commutator relation in type G₂

about: the tangent-space form of Ad(exp X) = exp(ad X) on a finite-dimensional real Lie group: the tangent adjoint action along the one-parameter subgroup generated by X and the operator exponential of ad X solve the same linear ODE with the same initial value, so uniqueness identifies them. This integrates the infinitesimal statement announced earlier (TauCeti#2840), which gave only the derivative of Ad at the identity.
name: Ad of the exponential is the exponential of ad

about: the nine irreducible crystallographic families are assembled into one construction indexed by a valid Dynkin type, with proofs that the datum realizes its indexing Cartan type and that its coroots span the cocharacter lattice (Bourbaki, *Lie Groups and Lie Algebras* IV–VI, Plates I–IX). The last missing family was E₇, whose 126 coroots are proved to exhaust the norm-two vectors rather than tabulated (TauCeti#3461); E₈ was announced earlier.
name: A pinned simply connected root datum for every Dynkin type

about: a subgroup of a rational representation stable under a Kostant ℤ-form contains every joint weight component of each of its elements, hence is the direct sum of the lattices it cuts out of the weight spaces (Humphreys, Lemma 27.1). The projector has to be built inside the form, from the binomial coefficients of the integer translates of a Cartan vector and Newton's forward-difference formula: the Lagrange interpolation projector has rational coefficients and need not preserve an integral structure.
name: Admissible lattices decompose into weight components

about: for squarefree d not a rational square, every prime of 𝒪_K with K = ℚ(√d) is unramified in the compositum of the quadratic fields attached to the prime discriminants dividing the fundamental discriminant of d, including p = 2 and the primes dividing d. For d < 0 the candidate is therefore an everywhere-unramified abelian extension of K, hence inside its Hilbert class field; maximality and Gal(K_gen/K) ≅ Cl(K)/Cl(K)² remain.
name: The candidate genus field is unramified over ℚ(√d) at the finite places

about: for a commutative Hopf algebra of finite type over an algebraically closed field, the Hopf ideal cutting out the connected component of the counit point is stable under conjugation (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, Prop. 2.37). The component group is then the fppf quotient by it, with H(k)/H⁰(k) identified with the connected components of Spec H and so finite (TauCeti#3496); representability of that quotient and its finite étaleness remain.
name: The identity component of an affine group is normal

about: weight-n purity as Deligne's opposedness condition on a bounded decreasing filtration F, that F p and the conjugate of F(n + 1 − p) are complementary for every p, with the pieces H^(p,n−p), the proof that conjugation exchanges H^(p,n−p) and H^(n−p,p), and the rank-one Tate structures ℤ(m) of weight −2m carrying the single nonzero piece H^(−m,−m) (Deligne, *Théorie de Hodge II*, §1.2.1). The conjugation is constructed, not assumed, as a canonical lattice-induced involution on an abstract complexification (TauCeti#3462); the internal-direct-sum decomposition is a separate target.
name: Pure Hodge structures

about: for an even nondegenerate integral lattice the half-norm q_L(x + L) = B(x, x)/2 mod ℤ descends to A_L = Lᵛ/L, evenness being exactly what makes it independent of the representative; its polar form is the discriminant pairing B(x, y) mod ℤ, it is nondegenerate, and it is functorial under isometries (Nikulin, §1.1). The ℚ/ℤ-valued pairing is TauCeti#3469, the order formula #A_L = |det Gram(L)| is TauCeti#3474, and the unimodularity equivalences TauCeti#3473.
name: The discriminant form of an even lattice

about: over a commutative ring A, the subgroup E(A) = ⟨xᵢ(t)⟩ of automorphisms of A ⊗ M generated by the divided-power exponentials of the distinguished root vectors on a Kostant-stable lattice M, functorial in A, with the endomorphism induced by the pⁿ-power Frobenius that a Steinberg map is built from, injective once the value ring is reduced (Carter, *Simple Groups of Lie Type*, §4.4). Identifying E(k) with all points of the Chevalley–Demazure group scheme is not claimed.
name: The elementary Chevalley group

about: over any field, GL₂ = B ⊔ BwB for the Borel subgroup B of upper-triangular matrices and the Weyl element w = (0 1; 1 0): B has exactly two double cosets, B and w together generate GL₂, and over 𝔽_q the big cell BwB has q²(q−1)² elements (Humphreys, *Linear Algebraic Groups*, §28.3); this is the double-coset input the Mackey criterion needs for the principal series below.
name: The Bruhat decomposition of GL₂

about: for a root pairing with a base, w · x = w(x + ρ) − ρ; unlike the linear action, which is free only on the open chamber, no nontrivial Weyl-group element fixes a dominant weight under the dot action, so distinct dominant weights lie in distinct dot orbits and each is reached by a unique group element (Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*, §23.3) — the separation statement the Harish-Chandra theory of central characters runs on.
name: The dot action of the Weyl group is free on the closed dominant chamber

about: for characters α, β of 𝔽_qˣ, the representation Ind_B^{GL₂}(α ⊗ β) induced from the Borel subgroup, of dimension q + 1, with the character of B inflated from the split torus and distinct pairs (α, β) giving distinct characters; the irreducibility criterion α ≠ β and the Steinberg constituent at α = β are not yet proved (Fulton–Harris, *Representation Theory*, §5.2).
name: The principal series of GL₂(𝔽_q)

about: for a module M of finite length over any ring, [M : S] counts the composition factors isomorphic to S; every composition series from ⊥ to ⊤ computes the same number (Lang, *Algebra*, I §3, Jordan–Hölder), it depends only on the isomorphism classes of M and S, and it is the invariant the Cartan matrix cᵢⱼ = [Pᵢ : Sⱼ] of a finite-dimensional algebra is defined by.
name: The Jordan–Hölder multiplicity of a simple module

about: a monoid acting by unipotent endomorphisms (each ρ(g) − 1 nilpotent) on a nonzero finite-dimensional vector space over any field fixes a nonzero vector (Borel, *Linear Algebraic Groups*, Prop. 4.8); hence a reduced affine group of finite type over an algebraically closed field has only unipotent points iff it is a closed subgroup of some upper-unitriangular Uₙ (Springer §2.4).
name: Kolchin's common fixed vector theorem

about: over a separably closed field of characteristic ≠ 2, the Clifford algebra of a nondegenerate quadratic form on a 2l-dimensional space is the matrix algebra M_{2^l}(F), by a dimension count against the Fock model ⋀W of a polarization V = W ⊕ W′; the odd-dimensional case is not yet treated (Fulton–Harris §20.1).
name: The structure theorem for even-dimensional Clifford algebras

about: for a split semisimple Lie algebra in characteristic zero with a base of its root system, the simple-root sl₂-triples satisfy (ad eᵢ)^{1 − ⟨αⱼ, αᵢ∨⟩} eⱼ = 0, so L is a quotient of the Serre algebra `Matrix.ToLieAlgebra` of its Cartan matrix by a map sending Hᵢ to αᵢ∨; injectivity of that map is not yet proved (Humphreys §18.1).
name: Serre's relations in a split semisimple Lie algebra

about: for a normalised family of root vectors x_α with ⁅x_α, x_{−α}⁆ = α∨, a Lie automorphism ω with ω(x_α) = −x_{−α} and ω = −1 on the Cartan subalgebra exists iff every structure constant N(α, β) is a Chevalley integer ±(p + 1), via the invariant N(α, β)·N(−α, −β) = −(p + 1)², and is then unique; producing an integrally normalised family, the other half of the Chevalley basis theorem, remains (Humphreys §25.2).
name: The Chevalley involution from integral structure constants

about: for a finite-dimensional Lie algebra with nondegenerate Killing form, Ω = Σᵢ xᵢ yᵢ ∈ U(L), with (yᵢ) the Killing-dual basis of (xᵢ), is independent of the basis and central in the enveloping algebra; its eigenvalue ⟨λ + ρ, λ + ρ⟩ − ⟨ρ, ρ⟩ on highest weight modules is a separate target (Humphreys §6.2; Bourbaki, *Lie*, I §3.7).
name: The Casimir element is central

about: the Bender–Knuth involution on semistandard tableaux of a fixed shape exchanges the multiplicities of v and v + 1 and fixes the others; reindexing the tableau generating function of TauCeti#2156 along it swaps adjacent variables, which generate Sₙ, so s_μ lies in the symmetric subalgebra (Bender–Knuth 1972; Stanley, EC2 §7.10).
name: Schur polynomials are symmetric, by the Bender–Knuth involution

about: a function completely monotone on (0, ∞) is the Laplace transform of a unique positive measure on ℝ≥0, now possibly infinite: the finite-measure form of TauCeti#2174 assumed continuity up to 0, and dropping it admits 1/t = ∫₀^∞ e^{−tx} dx, represented by Lebesgue measure (Widder, *The Laplace Transform*, Ch. IV Thm 12a).
name: The Hausdorff–Bernstein–Widder theorem on the open half-line

about: for a pure Hodge structure of weight n given by a bounded opposed filtration F (TauCeti#3520), the components H^{p,n−p} = F^p ∩ conj F^{n−p} are independent, span the complexification, and recover F^p = ⊕_{q ≥ p} H^{q,n−q} — the internal direct sum the earlier announcement left open (Deligne, *Théorie de Hodge II*, §1.2.1).
name: The Hodge decomposition

about: for a nondegenerate integral lattice L with discriminant group A_L = L^∨/L, the integral overlattices L ≤ M ≤ L^∨ correspond order-isomorphically to the subgroups of A_L on which the discriminant bilinear form vanishes, and for L even the even overlattices to those on which q_L : A_L → ℚ/ℤ vanishes (Nikulin, *Integral symmetric bilinear forms*, Prop. 1.4.1).
name: Nikulin's overlattice correspondence

about: for p ∣ N the slash sum Σ_{b<p} f ∣_k (1 b; 0 p) descends to ℂ-linear endomorphisms of M_k(Γ₁(N)) and S_k(Γ₁(N)) — the classical T_p at p ∣ N, the modern U_p — preserving each nebentypus space M_k(N, χ), S_k(N, χ), with a_m(T_p f) = a_{pm}(f) on q-expansions; the case p ∤ N, where a second coset adds χ(p)p^{k−1}a_{m/p}(f), is not yet built (Diamond–Shurman §5.2–5.3).
name: The Hecke operator at p ∣ N on modular forms

about: covers by members of a basis of the opens of X form a coverage on Opens X generating the usual Grothendieck topology, so a presheaf valued in any category is a sheaf iff it satisfies the sheaf condition for basis covers alone — the construction Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Sites.Coverage` docstring lists as an open project — and sheafhood on Spa(A, A⁺) is decided by rational covers (Stacks Tag 009H).
name: Sheaves are detected on a basis

about: `IsCoupling π μ ν`: a measure on X × Y with marginals μ and ν, stated for arbitrary measures, plus the bundled space of couplings of two probability measures; invariance under swap, pushforward and measurable equivalences, existence for finite measures iff the total masses agree, and uniqueness of the coupling out of a Dirac mass — the primitive object of the optimal-transport roadmap (Villani, *Optimal Transport*, Ch. 1).
name: Couplings of two measures

about: `Place k F`: a normalised discrete valuation of F/k, surjective onto ℤ and trivial on the constants, with its valuation ring 𝒪_P proved a DVR, the order function ord_P with the strict triangle inequality, the residue field F_P and degree [F_P : k], and a place determined by its valuation ring (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, §1.1).
name: Places of an algebraic function field

about: C⁺, the composite of the Bernstein–Gelfand–Ponomarev reflection functors along a sink-admissible ordering of the vertices, an endofunctor of the representations of a finite quiver; an indecomposable representation with finite-dimensional vertex spaces is either annihilated at some stage or carried to an indecomposable with dim(C⁺M) = c·dim M for the Coxeter transformation c — the engine of the BGP proof of Gabriel's theorem, whose height-descent argument is still to come (Bernstein–Gelfand–Ponomarev 1973).
name: The Coxeter functor of a quiver

about: `Graphon Ω μ`, a symmetric measurable kernel Ω × Ω → [0, 1] on a probability space; the homomorphism density t(F, W) = ∫ Π_{ij ∈ E(F)} W(x_i, x_j) dμ^{V(F)} of a finite simple graph, in [0, 1] with t(F, W_p) = p^{e(F)} for the constant graphon; and the cut norm ‖K‖_□ = sup_{S,T} |∫_{S×T} K| of a bounded symmetric kernel, a seminorm with ‖K‖_□ ≤ ∫|K| (Lovász, *Large Networks and Graph Limits*, §7.1, §8.2).
name: Graphons, homomorphism densities and the cut norm

about: at a nondegenerate critical point x of a smooth f : E → ℝ on a Banach space there is a chart ψ, smooth in both directions, with f(y) = f(x) + ½·D²f(x)(ψy, ψy) on its whole source — the Morse–Palais lemma, proved by Palais's square-root argument (Palais, Bull. AMS 75, 1969).
name: The Morse lemma

about: over a path-connected, locally path-connected, semilocally simply connected base, monodromy is an equivalence of categories from connected covering spaces to fibrewise transitive actions of the fundamental groupoid; the new half is reconstruction, quotienting the universal cover by a stabiliser (Hatcher §1.3).
name: The classification of connected covering spaces

about: W^{1,p}_0(Ω) now exists as the closure of C_c^∞(Ω) in the weak-derivative Sobolev space, and ‖u‖_p ≤ (b − a)·‖∇u‖_p holds on all of it when Ω lies between two hyperplanes at distance b − a, with the corollary ‖u‖_p ≤ 2R·‖∇u‖_p on a bounded Ω (Evans §5.6); the estimate announced earlier held for a single test function on a slab.
name: The Poincaré inequality on W^{1,p}_0(Ω)

about: an imaginary quadratic field with t ramified rational primes has 2-rank Cl(K) ≤ t − 1, via the counting step of the ambiguous class number formula: every 2-torsion class contains a conjugation-stable ideal (integral Hilbert 90, TauCeti#3796), and every such ideal is a product of ramified primes up to a rational ideal (Cox, *Primes of the Form x² + ny²*, Ch. 3).
name: The genus-theory bound on the 2-rank of an imaginary quadratic class group

about: every double coset of the Hecke triple (Γ₁(N), Δ₀(N)) now acts as a ℂ-linear endomorphism of M_k(Γ₁(N)) and S_k(Γ₁(N)) through Shimura's right-coset decomposition (Shimura, Prop. 3.37), and the normalisation lemma identifies the coset of diag(1, p) at p ∣ N with the classical U_p announced earlier (Diamond–Shurman, Prop. 5.2.1).
name: Hecke operators at every congruence level

about: for a finite quiver Q over a field k, the category of representations of Q is equivalent to the category of left kQ-modules, the new half being essential surjectivity via the kQ-action on ⨁_v M_v (Assem–Simson–Skowroński, Ch. III).
name: Representations of a quiver are modules over its path algebra

about: the generalized residue theorem announced earlier for one closed curve now holds for a null-homologous integer cycle of piecewise-C¹ immersions passing through the poles: the Cauchy principal value along the cycle is 2πi·Σ_s n_s(C)·Res_s f with non-integer generalized winding numbers, the form the paper states.
name: The Hungerbühler–Wasem residue theorem for cycles

about: over any field of characteristic p, the relative Frobenius F : W → W⁽ᵖ⁾ of a Weierstrass curve into its Frobenius twist, purely inseparable of degree p (Silverman, AEC II.2.11); the Frobenius isogeny announced earlier was the absolute q-power self-isogeny over a finite field.
name: The relative Frobenius isogeny

about: restricted to a normal subgroup, an irreducible representation has all its irreducible constituents occurring with hom spaces of one common dimension, the common multiplicity e over a splitting field (Isaacs, *Character Theory of Finite Groups*, Thm 6.2); this completes the single-orbit form announced earlier, with the packaged decomposition into e copies of the conjugates still to come.
name: Clifford's theorem, common-multiplicity half

about: an augmentation produces a class spanning a free 𝔽₂[U]-tower in the characteristic-two lattice homology of every negative-definite plumbing graph, the structure whose graded bottom carries Némethi's d-invariant; a companion result confines all homology below the top cubical degree (TauCeti#3833), while gradings and ℤ[U] signs are still to come.
name: Némethi's lattice homology of a negative-definite plumbing is nonzero

about: the primal optimal-transport functional, the infimum of ∫ c dπ over the couplings π of two measures, with the predicate cutting out optimal plans and its elementary calculus (Villani, *Topics in Optimal Transportation*, Ch. 1); the number the roadmap's existence, duality and Wasserstein layers are stated against.
name: The Kantorovich transport cost

about: the Grothendieck group cut out by [Y] − [X] − [Z] over the conflations of an exact structure, with its universal property and functoriality, alongside the split K₀ of an additive category identified with the group completion of the monoid of isomorphism classes (TauCeti#3795; Weibel, *The K-book*, Ch. II).
name: K₀ of a Quillen exact category

about: the Hodge–Riemann conditions on an integral bilinear form ((−1)ⁿ-symmetry, F^p ⊥ F^{n+1−p}, positivity of i^{p−q}·Q(x, x̄) on H^{p,q}), with the Tate structure as a polarized witness, together with the Weil operator C acting by i^{p−q} with C² = (−1)ⁿ (TauCeti#3870) — the two inputs the semisimplicity of polarizable Hodge structures runs through (Voisin, *Hodge Theory and Complex Algebraic Geometry I*, §7.1).
name: Polarizations of pure Hodge structures

about: the Y-coordinate half of the multiplication-by-n formula on a Weierstrass curve, completing the classical (φ, ψ) pair through 2ωₙ = ψcₙ − a₁φₙψₙ − a₃ψₙ³ (Silverman, AEC Exercise 3.7), the route the roadmap pins for Nagell–Lutz.
name: The ω division polynomials

about: for K = ℚ(√d), d < −1 squarefree, the classes of the t ramified primes in Cl(𝒪_K) satisfy no relation beyond the one known one, so they generate a subgroup of order exactly 2^(t−1), giving the genus-theory lower bound 2-rank Cl(𝒪_K) ≥ t − 1; with the upper bound announced earlier (TauCeti#3796, TauCeti#3884) the 2-rank is now exactly t − 1 (Cox, *Primes of the Form x² + ny²*, §3).
name: The ramified primes of an imaginary quadratic field span exactly 2^(t−1) classes

about: over a split semisimple Lie algebra, two irreducible modules carrying highest weight vectors of weights λ and μ are isomorphic exactly when λ = μ, with no finite-dimensionality assumed, and every highest weight module has a greatest proper submodule with irreducible quotient, so L(λ) is well defined (Humphreys, *BGG Category 𝒪*, §1).
name: Irreducible highest weight modules are classified by their weight

about: the Conway-normalised Δ_V = T^(−g) · det(T·V − Vᵀ) over Laurent polynomials, symmetric under t ↦ t⁻¹, invariant under congruence and under the two enlargements that generate S-equivalence, with Δ(1) = det(V − Vᵀ), Δ = 1 for the unknot, and the classical values t − 1 + t⁻¹ and −t + 3 − t⁻¹ for the trefoil and figure-eight; the input is a Seifert matrix; a knot-embedding front end is separate later work (Lickorish, *An Introduction to Knot Theory*, Ch. 6).
name: The Alexander polynomial of a Seifert matrix

about: a Dirichlet series with nonnegative coefficients has a singularity at its finite abscissa of absolute convergence: no function differentiable on a disc around σ agrees with the series immediately to its right (Hardy–Riesz, *The General Theory of Dirichlet's Series*).
name: Landau's theorem for Dirichlet series with nonnegative coefficients

about: every torus over a field is reductive, in arbitrary characteristic: every smooth unipotent closed subgroup of the geometric fibre is trivial (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, 12.41).
name: Tori are reductive

about: for a polarized quadratic space with no line summand, the even Clifford subalgebra is End(S⁺) × End(S⁻) for the two half-spin representations, so invariant subspaces obey a strict dichotomy and every intertwiner between S⁺ and S⁻ vanishes, refining the full structure theorem Cl(Q) ≅ M_{2^l}(F) announced earlier (Fulton–Harris, §20).
name: The even Clifford structure theorem on half-spinors

about: the unit sphere of a real normed space of rank greater than two, in particular Sⁿ for n ≥ 2, is simply connected, by piecewise-linear interpolation, point omission and radial projection with no smoothing or simplicial approximation; this makes the library's π₁(ℝPⁿ) ≃ ℤ/2 unconditional, and the same sphere theorem is concurrently being formalised in mathlib4#28246 by a different route.
name: The unit sphere is simply connected above rank two

about: the quotient map of a profinite group by a closed subgroup admits a continuous section normalised at the identity, via a Zorn-and-Cantor construction of a closed transversal (Ribes–Zalesskii, *Profinite Groups*, Prop. 2.2.2).
name: Continuous sections of profinite quotients

about: the orbit space of a free, properly discontinuous action of G on a weakly contractible space is a K(G,1), a path-connected cover of a K(G,1) is a K(H,1) for the subgroup H it recovers, and a space is aspherical exactly when its universal cover is weakly contractible — the machinery producing new K(G,1)s from old (Hatcher, §1.B).
name: The K(G,1) recognition principles

about: every rational representation of GL n ℂ is the internal direct sum of its weight spaces under the diagonal torus, every joint eigencharacter being a monomial t ↦ ∏ tᵢ^(lᵢ), by Laurent expansion of the action and Artin's independence of characters (Jantzen, *Representations of Algebraic Groups*, I.2).
name: The weight-space decomposition of rational GL n representations

about: the Grothendieck group of an essentially small abelian category, universal for invariants additive on short exact sequences and satisfying [X] − [Y] = [ker f] − [coker f] for every morphism f, together with the triangulated K₀ of a pretriangulated category, with [Y] = [X] + [Z] over distinguished triangles and [X⟦n⟧] = (−1)ⁿ[X]; these complete the four Grothendieck groups begun with the split and exact cases (TauCeti#3795, TauCeti#3829).
name: Abelian and triangulated K₀

about: for a cocharacter λ : 𝔾ₘ → G of an affine group scheme, the subgroup functors P(λ), U(λ) and Z(λ) defined by limits along λ, with the Levi decomposition P(λ)(A) = U(λ)(A) ⋊ Z(λ)(A) on points — the dynamic route to parabolics that needs no root data (Conrad–Gabber–Prasad, *Pseudo-reductive Groups*, §2.1).
name: The dynamic parabolic, unipotent and Levi subgroups of a cocharacter

about: the two symmetries of a doubly indexed random array, law invariant under independent row and column permutations or only simultaneous ones, separated by an explicit witness, with de Finetti for the rows: the rows of a separately exchangeable array are conditionally i.i.d. — the first step of the classical route to the Aldous–Hoover representation (Kallenberg, *Probabilistic Symmetries and Invariance Principles*, Ch. 7).
name: Separately and jointly exchangeable arrays

about: the path law of the Markov chain with initial law ν and transition kernel κ, built on Mathlib's Ionescu–Tulcea trajectory measure, with the Markov property, the marginal recursion, and the mass of a finite path as initial weight times transition weights (Kallenberg, *Foundations of Modern Probability*, Ch. 8).
name: The homogeneous Markov chain of a transition kernel
