about: a `C^n` map between boundaryless Banach manifolds (`1 ≤ n`) whose `mfderiv` at a point is a continuous linear equivalence is a `C^n` local diffeomorphism at that point — the converse of Mathlib's `IsLocalDiffeomorphAt.mfderivToContinuousLinearEquiv`, completing the characterisation of local diffeomorphisms by invertibility of the differential (Lang, *Differential and Riemannian Manifolds*).
name: The inverse function theorem for manifolds

about: for K = ℚ(√d) with d < −1 squarefree, the 2-rank of Cl(𝒪_K) equals t − 1, t the number of ramified rational primes: the upper bound of TauCeti#3884 and the lower bound of TauCeti#3912 joined into the closed genus-theory equality (Cox, *Primes of the Form x² + ny²*, §3; Lemmermeyer, *Reciprocity Laws*, §2.2).
name: Gauss's 2-rank formula for imaginary quadratic fields

about: over a path-connected, locally path-connected, semilocally simply connected base, monodromy is an equivalence of categories `CoveringSpace X ≌ (FundamentalGroupoid X ⥤ Type)`, extending the connected classification of TauCeti#3898 to all covering spaces; the disconnected case is rebuilt through a balanced-product construction over the universal cover (Brown, *Topology and Groupoids*; Spanier, Ch. 2).
name: The classification of covering spaces

about: the first concrete instance of the parametrised elementary-group machinery of TauCeti#3506: for a Chevalley system the divided-power exponentials x_α(t) act on the adjoint Chevalley lattice over every commutative ring A, generating Carter's E(A), with the Chevalley commutator relation ⁅x_α(s), x_β(t)⁆ = x_{α+β}(N s t) for an integer structure constant N = ±(p + 1) (Carter, *Simple Groups of Lie Type*, §4.4, Theorem 5.2.2).
name: The adjoint elementary Chevalley group

about: on the universal Weierstrass curve, n • (X, Y) = (φₙ/ψₙ², ωₙ/ψₙ³) for every n ≠ 0, and distinct multiples are distinct points: the closed form for multiplication-by-n that the ω division polynomials of TauCeti#3862 were built for (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, Exercise 3.7), ported from J. Xu and D. K. Angdinata's Nagell–Lutz development in AINTLIB.
name: The division-polynomial formula for n • P

about: adjoining two generators of square −1 tensors with the quaternions and swaps the signature, `Cliff(p, q + 2) ≅ Cliff(q, p) ⊗ ℍ`: the companion of the library's M₂(ℝ) recurrences and a standard step towards the mod-8 classification of real Clifford algebras, which remains later work (Lawson–Michelsohn, *Spin Geometry*, Ch. I).
name: The quaternionic recurrence for real Clifford algebras

about: the double coset Γ₁(N)·diag(1, p)·Γ₁(N) splits into its p + 1 right cosets at a good prime (Diamond–Shurman, Proposition 5.2.1), giving Tₚ f = Σ_{b<p} f∣ₖ(1 b; 0 p) + (⟨p⟩ f)∣ₖ(p 0; 0 1) on `M_k(Γ₁(N))` and `S_k(Γ₁(N))` with no case split on the prime — at p ∣ N the diamond term vanishes and the formula degenerates to the Uₚ of TauCeti#3817.
name: The classical Hecke operator Tₚ at every prime

about: on a module generated by a highest weight vector of weight λ, the Casimir element of TauCeti#3750 acts by the scalar ⟨λ + ρ, λ + ρ⟩ − ⟨ρ, ρ⟩, the eigenvalue flagged there as a separate target and the key input to Weyl's complete reducibility (Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*, §§22–23).
name: The Casimir eigenvalue on a highest weight module

about: Π_k(Q), the path algebra of the doubled quiver modulo the relation Σ_a (a a* − a* a), with the vertexwise relations ρ_v proved to span the same two-sided ideal, so a map out of Π_k(Q) is checked one vertex at a time (Gelfand–Ponomarev; Crawley-Boevey's lectures on quiver representations).
name: The preprojective algebra of a quiver

about: piecewise-linear maps of real topological vector spaces (locally, a finite cover by convex polyhedra on each of which the map is continuous affine) satisfy Mathlib's pregroupoid laws, so PL manifolds — boundary and corner models included — are now `HasGroupoid M (PLGroupoid I)`, with the forgetful inclusion PL ⇒ Top (Rourke–Sanderson, *Introduction to Piecewise-Linear Topology*).
name: The PL structure groupoid

about: the ordered product ι v₁ ⋯ ι vₙ of a pairwise orthogonal spanning list is central for odd n, anticommutes with every generator for even n, and squares to (−1)^(n choose 2) · Q(v₁) ⋯ Q(vₙ), over any commutative ring with no invertibility of 2 — the extra central element behind the odd-dimensional Clifford centre (Lawson–Michelsohn, *Spin Geometry*, Ch. I).
name: The volume element of a Clifford algebra

about: a sufficiently differentiable map between finite-dimensional real normed spaces, with no relation between the two dimensions, has a Haar-null set of critical values, so its regular values are dense; this completes, by Milnor's Fubini induction, the theorem whose one-dimensional, equal-dimension and vanishing-derivative slices were announced earlier (Milnor, *Topology from the Differentiable Viewpoint*, §3).
name: The Morse–Sard theorem in finite dimensions

about: for a lower semicontinuous cost on Polish spaces the Kantorovich infimum is attained: the couplings of two probability measures form a weakly compact set by tightness and Prokhorov's theorem, and the direct method produces an optimal plan, with attainment separated from finiteness of the optimal value (Villani, *Optimal Transport: Old and New*, Thm 4.1).
name: Existence of an optimal transport plan

about: for a divergence-form operator `L u = -∂ⱼ(aⁱʲ ∂ᵢu) + bⁱ ∂ᵢu + c u` with coercive energy form and `f ∈ L²(Ω)`, exactly one `u ∈ H¹₀(Ω)` satisfies `a(u, v) = ∫ f v` for all `v`, with the energy estimate `‖u‖ ≤ ‖f‖/C`, by Lax–Milgram; instantiated for the Poisson equation `-Δu = f` on bounded-geometry domains (Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, Ch. 6).
name: The Dirichlet problem has a unique weak solution

about: the energy form of a uniformly elliptic divergence-form operator with bounded drift satisfies `(λ/2)‖∇u‖² − (β²/2λ)‖u‖²_{L²} ≤ a(u, u)` on `H¹(Ω)`, the lower bound behind the coercivity the Dirichlet theorem consumes (Evans, Ch. 6).
name: Gårding's inequality

about: for `K/ℚ` finite Galois the inertia subgroups of the primes of `𝓞 K` generate `Gal(K/ℚ)`, since their fixed field would otherwise be an everywhere-unramified extension of `ℚ`, which Minkowski's discriminant bound forbids; the recorded consequence is the genus-theory step that an abelian extension of a number field unramified at all finite places has Galois group of exponent dividing the base degree (Serre, *Topics in Galois Theory*, §4.4).
name: The inertia subgroups generate the Galois group of a number field

about: a locally flat embedded `(n−1)`-manifold in an `n`-manifold has two-sided product neighbourhoods locally, with the converse over domains charted on the model space; the local half of Brown's collaring theorem, whose global statement is a separate later target (M. Brown, *Ann. of Math.* 75 (1962)).
name: Locally flat embeddings of codimension one are locally bicollared

about: the places of `k(x)` are exactly the monic irreducible polynomials together with the place at infinity, with residue field `k[X]/(q)` and degree `deg q` at the finite place of `q` and degree one at infinity, so the degree-one places are `ℙ¹(k) = k ∪ {∞}`; built on Mathlib's Ostrowski-type classification of the valuations of `k(X)` (Stichtenoth, Prop. 1.2.1 and Thm. 1.2.2).
name: The places of the rational function field, classified

about: jointly with its directing measure, an exchangeable sequence in a standard Borel space is the coordinatewise image of an i.i.d. uniform sequence under one fixed measurable map, the same map for every process, and conversely every such coded law is exchangeable — upgrading the conditional-law form of de Finetti announced earlier to a functional representation (Kallenberg, *Probabilistic Symmetries and Invariance Principles*, Prop. 1.4).
name: The coding representation of an exchangeable sequence

about: a rational weight filtration together with a Hodge filtration on the complexification whose weight-graded pieces carry pure Hodge structures, with the comparison `ℂ ⊗ grᵂ_k ≅ (W_k)_ℂ/(W_{k−1})_ℂ` proved, pure structures embedded as one-weight mixed ones, and the Tate structure as the first example; Deligne's `I^{p,q}` bigrading and strictness are later targets (Deligne, *Théorie de Hodge II*; Peters–Steenbrink).
name: Mixed Hodge structures

about: the group presented by the braid-word relations of a Coxeter matrix, with its universal property and canonical surjection onto the Coxeter group, and its type-A instance the braid group on `n` strands, mapping onto `Sₙ` with the pure braid group as kernel and nonabelian from three strands on; braid groups are also being formalised upstream in mathlib4#32941 (Brieskorn–Saito; Birman).
name: The Artin–Tits group of a Coxeter matrix, and the braid group

about: `M(λ)`, the quotient of `U(L)` by the left ideal generated by the kernel of the Borel character, with its universal property: every highest weight module of weight `λ` is a quotient of `M(λ)`, and `M(λ)` has a unique irreducible quotient `L(λ)`; nonvanishing of `M(λ)` is pinned to the linear-independence half of PBW, still open, and is proved for `λ = 0` (Humphreys, §20).
name: The Verma module

about: `erf` and `erfc` with oddness, strict monotonicity, the limits at both infinities and the derivative, giving the Gaussian cumulative distribution function in closed form, `cdf = (1 + erf((x − m)/√(2v)))/2`; the declarations follow the shapes of the open mathlib4#34053 so they can be swapped out when it lands (DLMF, Ch. 7).
name: The error function

about: the critical values of a C^k Fredholm map from an open subset of a second-countable Banach space to a complete normed space are meagre, so its regular values are residual and dense; at the threshold k ≥ (dim ker)² + 1, not yet Smale's sharp k > index (Smale, Amer. J. Math. 87 (1965)).
name: The Sard–Smale theorem

about: for A, B ∈ ℤ, a nonzero rational torsion point on y² = x³ + Ax + B has integer coordinates with y = 0 or y² ∣ Δ (Silverman, AEC VIII.7.1); the long-model form over the fraction field of any UFD — integral except at order two, where 4x, 8y are integral, with ψ₂² ∣ 4Δ — is TauCeti#4348 and TauCeti#4358.
name: The Nagell–Lutz theorem

about: TL_n(R, δ) by generators e₁, …, e_{n−1} and its three relations, shown not to collapse, and σᵢ ↦ a·1 + a⁻¹eᵢ at δ = −(a² + a⁻²), satisfying the braid relations and giving a nontrivial B_n → TL_n(R, δ)ˣ (Jones, Bull. AMS 12 (1985)); the Markov trace, hence the Jones polynomial, is not yet built.
name: The Temperley–Lieb algebra and the Jones representation of the braid group

about: a function on [0, ∞) right-continuous at 0 whose mixed forward differences with nonnegative steps satisfy (−1)ⁿ Δ_{h₁}⋯Δ_{hₙ} f ≥ 0 is the Laplace transform of a unique finite measure on ℝ≥0, and conversely, so Hausdorff's difference condition is equivalent to the smooth complete monotonicity of TauCeti#2174 (Widder, *The Laplace Transform*, Ch. IV).
name: The Hausdorff–Bernstein–Widder theorem in finite-difference form

about: each class in Br(K) is represented by a finite-dimensional central division K-algebra, unique up to K-algebra isomorphism (Gille–Szamuely §2.4), and the kernel of Br(K) → Br(L) is exactly the classes split by L (TauCeti#4210).
name: Every Brauer class contains a unique division algebra

about: every rational Hodge substructure of a polarizable pure Hodge structure has an orthogonal complement for the polarizing form which is again a rational Hodge substructure and complements it over ℚ and over ℂ (Peters–Steenbrink, *Mixed Hodge Structures*, Ch. 2).
name: Polarizable rational Hodge structures are semisimple

about: for a bounded cochain complex over an abelian category the alternating sum of the classes of its terms equals that of its cohomology, for every invariant additive on short exact sequences, so the K₀-valued Euler characteristic is a quasi-isomorphism invariant (Weibel, *The K-book*, II.6.6).
name: The Euler–Poincaré theorem in abelian K₀

about: for N ⊲ G finite and W irreducible over a splitting field, Res_N χ_W = e · Σ_g χ_{gV} over a transversal of the inertia group of a constituent V, e the common multiplicity: the full identity, assembled from the single-orbit form of TauCeti#2667 and the multiplicity half of TauCeti#3766 (Isaacs, Thm 6.2).
name: Clifford's theorem, character form

about: under a liminf condition on the moving costs and a recovery-plan condition, optimal values converge to that of the limit problem and optimal plans accumulate only on its optimal plans (Villani, *Optimal Transport: Old and New*, Thm 5.20).
name: Stability of optimal transport

about: |t(F, U) − t(F, W)| ≤ e(F)·‖U − W‖□ for a finite simple graph F and graphons U, W on one probability space (Lovász, *Large Networks and Graph Limits*, 10.23); the coupling-primary cut distance δ□ is defined in TauCeti#4141, its triangle inequality still open.
name: The counting lemma for graphons

about: for isogenies φ : W₁ → W₂ and ψ : W₁ → W₃ of Weierstrass curves over any field, ψ = λ ∘ φ for a unique isogeny λ exactly when ψ*F(W₃) ⊆ φ*F(W₂) inside F(W₁), with no separability hypothesis (Silverman III.4.11, there separable); so a degree-one isogeny is an isomorphism.
name: The factorisation theorem for isogenies

about: over an algebraically closed field a linearly reductive affine group has no nontrivial normal unipotent closed subgroup, so a smooth geometrically connected affine group of finite type with linearly reductive geometric fibre is reductive, in every characteristic (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, 12.45).
name: Linearly reductive groups are reductive

about: for projectives relative to a Quillen exact structure: conflations K ↪ Q ↠ X and K' ↪ Q' ↠ X with projective middle terms have K ⊞ Q' ≅ K' ⊞ Q, and a conflation X ↪ Y ↠ Z with projective presentations of X and Z yields K ↪ Q_X ⊞ Q_Z ↠ Y with kernel an extension of the two syzygies (Bühler, *Exact categories*, §12).
name: Schanuel's lemma and the horseshoe lemma

about: the unreduced Burau representation B_n → GL_n(R) over any commutative ring and unit t, σᵢ ↦ the block [[1 − t, t], [1, 0]] on strands i, i + 1, with determinant (−t)^(exponent sum), specialising at t = 1 to the permutation representation (Birman, *Braids, Links, and Mapping Class Groups*); the reduced representation is not yet carved out.
name: The Burau representation

about: at every prime p and level Γ₁(N), aₘ(Tₚ f) = a_{pm}(f) + p^{k−1} a_{m/p}(⟨p⟩f), on M_k(N, χ) with p ∤ N the classical aₘ(Tₚ f) = a_{pm}(f) + χ(p) p^{k−1} a_{m/p}(f), and at p ∣ N the Uₚ case (Diamond–Shurman 5.2.2); hence the Tₚ-eigenvalue of a normalised eigenform is aₚ(f).
name: The Fourier-coefficient recurrence for Tₚ

about: for K = ℚ(√d), d squarefree with |d| > 1, of either signature, the 2-rank of the narrow class group Cl⁺(K) is at most t − 1, t the number of ramified rational primes (Lemmermeyer, *Reciprocity Laws*, §2.2); TauCeti#3884 had the imaginary case, and the matching lower bound for real fields is still open.
name: The first inequality of genus theory

about: I^{p,q} = (F^p ∩ W_{p+q}) ∩ (conj F^q ∩ W_{p+q} + Σ_{j≥2} conj F^{q−j+1} ∩ W_{p+q−j}), with I^{p,q} ≤ F^p ∩ W_{p+q}, I^{p,q} ≤ conj F^q modulo W_{p+q−2}, functoriality, and equal to the Hodge decomposition on a pure structure (Deligne, *Théorie de Hodge II*, 1.2.10); that ⊕ I^{p,q} is everything in general, and strictness, are the next steps.
name: Deligne's bigrading of a mixed Hodge structure

about: for an elliptic Weierstrass curve W over a field K, Mathlib's injective map W(K) → Cl(K[W]) sending an affine point to the class of its point ideal is surjective, so the group of rational points is the ideal class group of the affine coordinate ring, by a genus-one Riemann–Roch dimension count over K[W] (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, III.3.4–5).
name: The rational points of an elliptic curve are the class group of its coordinate ring

about: for a Noetherian domain A of Krull dimension at most one with fraction field K and any finite extension L/K, the integral closure of A in L is Noetherian, with no separability hypothesis on L/K and no claim that it is a finite A-module; Mathlib has the separable case via the trace pairing, and the general case runs on the length bound length_A(M/aM) ≤ dim_K V · length_A(A/aA) (Matsumura, *Commutative Ring Theory*, Thm 11.7).
name: The Krull–Akizuki theorem

about: an explicit isometry of integral lattices between E₈ and D₈⁺ = D₈ ∪ (s + D₈), built from Bourbaki's eight simple roots written in Conway–Sloane coordinates and closed by unimodularity of E₈ rather than by uniqueness of the even unimodular lattice of rank 8; the discriminant forms agree and H⊥/H is trivial for the spinor glue subgroup H (Conway–Sloane, *Sphere Packings, Lattices and Groups*, Ch. 4).
name: The spinor glue lattice D₈⁺ is the E₈ root lattice

about: for an irreducible unitary representation π of a compact group on a finite-dimensional complex inner product space, the indicator ∫ χ_π(g²) dg is 1, 0 or −1, being 1 exactly when Sym²V has a nonzero invariant, −1 exactly when Λ²V does, and 0 when neither; this extends the finite-group trichotomy of TauCeti#2206 to compact groups via Haar integration and Schur's lemma, while the reading of the three values as real, complex and quaternionic type is a separate step not yet taken (Bröcker–tom Dieck, *Representations of Compact Lie Groups*, II.6).
name: The Frobenius–Schur trichotomy for compact groups

about: for probability mass functions μ, ν on finite sets and an arbitrary real cost c, the minimum of ∑ c·A over transport plans A equals the maximum of ∑ φ dμ + ∑ ψ dν over potentials with φ_i + ψ_j ≤ c(i, j), both extrema are attained, and a plan and a feasible pair are simultaneously optimal exactly when the plan is concentrated on the contact set of the pair; strong duality comes from Mathlib's Sion minimax theorem, and the Polish-space duality is a later milestone (Villani, *Topics in Optimal Transportation*, Ch. 1).
name: Kantorovich duality on finite spaces

about: over every field and in every characteristic, GLₙ satisfies the geometric definition of reductivity: it is smooth and geometrically connected, and has no nontrivial connected normal smooth unipotent closed subgroup over the algebraic closure, since such a subgroup fixes a nonzero vector of the standard representation by Kolchin's theorem, normality makes the fixed space a subcomodule, and simplicity of the standard representation then makes it everything (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, §12; Springer, *Linear Algebraic Groups*, §2.4).
name: The general linear group is reductive

about: for an algebraic function field F/k over an arbitrary constant field and z ∈ F transcendental over k, deg (z)₀ = deg (z)∞ = [F : k(z)], so every principal divisor has degree zero, degree descends to the divisor class group, ℓ(D) = 0 when deg D < 0, and (TauCeti#4410) a degree-zero divisor is principal exactly when ℓ(D) ≥ 1, exactly when ℓ(D) = 1 over an exact constant field (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, Thm 1.4.11 and Cor. 1.4.12).
name: The product formula for algebraic function fields

about: in a Quillen exact category, for a class P of projectives containing 0 and closed under biproducts, the alternating class [Q₀] − [Q₁] + ⋯ of a finite P-resolution in K₀(P) depends only on the resolved object (Schanuel's lemma) and is additive on conflations (the horseshoe lemma), so the inclusion of P into the objects of finite P-dimension induces an isomorphism on exact K₀ with inverse the Euler class; the K₀ statement only, not Quillen's higher-K version (Quillen, *Higher algebraic K-theory I*, §4; Weibel, *The K-book*, II.7.6).
name: The resolution theorem for K₀ of an exact category

about: over a separably closed field of characteristic ≠ 2, the Clifford algebra of a nondegenerate quadratic form on a (2l+1)-dimensional space is M_{2^l}(F) × M_{2^l}(F) and its even subalgebra is M_{2^l}(F), completing the even-dimensional case of TauCeti#3655 by splitting along the central volume element and identifying the even part through a central idempotent of a simple ring (Lam, *Introduction to Quadratic Forms over Fields*, Ch. V; Fulton–Harris §20.1).
name: The structure theorem for odd-dimensional Clifford algebras

about: for V a finite-dimensional real inner product space, a function F on the involutive semigroup ℝ≥0 × V is positive definite, continuous and bounded exactly when it is the Laplace–Fourier transform of a unique finite measure on ℝ≥0 × V; the existence half is new and closes the semigroup-Bochner milestone by a fibrewise Hausdorff–Bernstein–Widder argument on the densities of the time slices, the uniqueness half having landed earlier (Berg–Christensen–Ressel, *Harmonic Analysis on Semigroups*, §4.2).
name: The Berg–Christensen–Ressel representation theorem

about: the augmentation subrepresentation of the permutation representation ℂ[GL₂/B] on the projective line: it has dimension q, its character at g is the number of B-cosets fixed by g less one, the boundary principal series Ind_B(1 ⊗ 1) of TauCeti#3549 has character 1 + χ_St, and ⟨χ_St, χ_St⟩ = 1 by the two Bruhat double cosets; irreducibility as a `Simple` object is not yet drawn from the norm-one identity (Fulton–Harris §5.2; Steinberg 1951).
name: The Steinberg representation of GL₂(𝔽_q)

about: the multiplicity function χ ↦ dim M_χ of a finite-dimensional module over a nilpotent Lie algebra with linear weights, as an element of the integral group algebra ℤ[𝔥*]; isomorphism invariant and additive on products, and for a Cartan subalgebra of a Killing-semisimple Lie algebra over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero its coefficients are the honest weight multiplicities, supported on integral weights and Weyl-invariant; multiplicativity on tensor products is the next step (Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*, §22.5).
name: The formal character of a finite-dimensional Lie module

about: 𝒦_X as an 𝒪_X-module sheaf, the pushforward of the structure sheaf of Spec K(X) along Spec K(X) → X, whose sections over every nonempty open are K(X) compatibly with restriction and into which 𝒪_X embeds as a subsheaf; the object Cartier divisors and 𝒪_X(D) are phrased in, with Mathlib supplying the function field but no sheaf carrying it (Hartshorne, *Algebraic Geometry*, II.6).
name: The sheaf of rational functions on an integral scheme

about: every Bernstein function f on [0, ∞) has the form f(λ) = a + bλ + ∫₀^∞ (1 − e^(−λt)) dμ(t) with a, b ≥ 0 and μ a measure on (0, ∞) with ∫ min(1, t) dμ < ∞, and conversely every such function is Bernstein (TauCeti#320 defined the class); uniqueness of the triplet (a, b, μ) is the next step (Schilling–Song–Vondraček, *Bernstein Functions*, Thm 3.2).
name: The Lévy–Khintchine representation of Bernstein functions

about: for an algebraic function field F/k the defect deg D − ℓ(D) is bounded over all divisors D, its maximum defines the genus g = max_D (deg D + 1 − ℓ(D)), and ℓ(D) ≥ deg D + 1 − g for every divisor, with equality once deg D is large when k is algebraically closed in F; the index of specialty i(D) = ℓ(D) − deg D − 1 + g is defined and vanishes in large degree, while Riemann–Roch itself waits on Weil differentials (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, I.4–I.5).
name: Riemann's theorem and the genus of a function field

about: for an irreducible unitary representation π of a compact group on a finite-dimensional complex inner product space, ν₂(π) = 1 exactly when π carries a nondegenerate invariant symmetric bilinear form, −1 exactly when it carries a nondegenerate invariant alternating one, and 0 exactly when it carries no nonzero invariant bilinear form at all; TauCeti#4313 had the trichotomy through invariants of Sym²V and Λ²V, and the reading as real, complex and quaternionic type remains a further step (Bump, *Lie Groups*, ch. 2).
name: The Frobenius–Schur indicator of a compact group, read off invariant forms

about: a family of subspaces H^p of a complex vector space with conjugation ω which is an internal direct sum, satisfies ω(H^p) = H^(n−p) and vanishes in low degree determines a pure Hodge structure of weight n with F^p = ⊕_(q ≥ p) H^q, and this is inverse to taking Hodge components, so pure Hodge structures of weight n are the same thing as their (p, q)-decompositions; TauCeti#3662 had the forward direction only (Deligne, *Théorie de Hodge II*, §1.2.1).
name: The Hodge decomposition as an equivalence

about: a finite-dimensional central simple algebra over a separably closed field K is K-isomorphic to M_n(K), by the Jacobson–Noether theorem applied to the division algebra in Artin–Wedderburn, so every separably closed extension of a field splits all of its central simple algebras; Mathlib has the algebraically closed case (Gille–Szamuely, *Central Simple Algebras and Galois Cohomology*, §2.2).
name: Central simple algebras over separably closed fields are matrix algebras

about: if M/ℚ is abelian, F ⊆ M is quadratic and M/F is unramified at every finite prime, then M = ℚ(√a₁, …, √aₙ) for squarefree integers aᵢ no nonempty product of which is a square, so [M : ℚ] = 2ⁿ; this is the field-theoretic half of the maximality of the genus field, whose arithmetic half — matching the aᵢ to prime discriminants — comes next (Cox, *Primes of the Form x² + ny²*, §6.A).
name: Unramified abelian extensions over a quadratic field are multiquadratic

about: the generalized winding number of the boundary of the upper half-disc of radius R is 1 at every point inside it, ½ at the origin and 0 outside, so for f holomorphic off a finite set {0} ∪ S with at worst simple poles there and S in the open half-disc, the Cauchy principal value of ∮ f along that boundary is 2πi Σ_(s ∈ S) Res_s f + πi Res₀ f, the pole on the contour counting half; the version along the real diameter with the arc subtracted is the form real improper integrals consume (Henrici, *Applied and Computational Complex Analysis* I, Thm 4.8f).
name: The half-disc residue theorem with enclosed poles

about: the sheaf 𝒦_X^×/𝒪_X^×, formed as a cokernel in sheaves of abelian groups rather than as a quotient of global sections, and its group of global sections Cartier(X) with the principal divisor map K(X)^× → Cartier(X); 𝒪_X(D) and the dictionary with line bundles are the next steps (Stacks 02AR; Hartshorne II.6).
name: Cartier divisors on an integral scheme

about: for E: y² = f(x) over a field K of characteristic ≠ 2, with A = K[X]/(f) and T the class of X, the map E(K) → A^×/(A^×)² sending (x, y) to the square class of x − T (corrected at the 2-torsion, where x − T is a zero divisor) is a group homomorphism, because the classes of three collinear points multiply to 1; that its kernel is 2E(K), the descent computing E(K)/2E(K), is the next step (ported from Michael Stoll's *EllipticCurves*; cf. Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, X.1).
name: The x − T map of an elliptic curve

about: a smooth homomorphism φ of finite-dimensional real Lie groups induces a Lie algebra homomorphism Lie(φ) on left-invariant derivations, its differential at the identity, with Lie(id) = id, Lie(ψ ∘ φ) = Lie(ψ) ∘ Lie(φ) and φ(exp X) = exp(Lie(φ) X) (Hall, *Lie Groups, Lie Algebras, and Representations*, ch. 3).
name: The Lie functor on morphisms

about: over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, every finite-dimensional module over a Lie algebra with nondegenerate Killing form is a direct sum of irreducible submodules, every Lie submodule having a complement (Humphreys, GTM 9, §6.3).
name: Weyl's complete reducibility theorem

about: over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, an irreducible module over a Killing-semisimple Lie algebra generated by a highest weight vector of weight λ is finite-dimensional if and only if λ is dominant integral (Humphreys, GTM 9, §21.2).
name: Irreducible highest weight modules are finite-dimensional exactly at dominant integral weights

about: in characteristic zero, V(m) ⊗ V(n) is the direct sum of explicit submodules isomorphic to V(m + n − 2k), 0 ≤ k ≤ min(m, n) (Fulton–Harris §11.2).
name: The Clebsch–Gordan rule for sl₂

about: for a continuous nonnegative cost on compact pseudometric spaces and probability measures μ, ν, inf_π ∫ c dπ over couplings equals the supremum of ∫φ dμ + ∫ψ dν over continuous (equally, integrable) potentials with φ(x) + ψ(y) ≤ c(x, y), extending the finite-space duality of 25 August (Villani, *Topics in Optimal Transportation*, Thm 1.3); attainment of the supremum is not claimed.
name: Strong Kantorovich duality on compact spaces

about: an irreducible complex representation of a finite group has ν₂ = 1 exactly when it is the complexification of a real representation; the new half builds the real structure from an invariant symmetric and an invariant Hermitian form, completing the trichotomy of 8 August (Serre, *Linear Representations of Finite Groups*, §13.2).
name: Frobenius–Schur indicator 1 means realizable over ℝ

about: over a path-connected, locally path-connected, semilocally simply connected base, the covering spaces with finite fibres form a Galois category (SGA 1) with the fibre over a basepoint as fibre functor.
name: Finite covering spaces form a Galois category

about: for a nonzero weight-k modular form on a finite-index Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ), Σ_P (2/|Stab_Γ P|)·ord_P f + Σ_c ord_c f = k·[SL₂(ℤ):Γ]/12, the cusp sum over the ⟨T⟩-orbits on SL₂(ℤ)/Γ with each order read in its own width; the level-one case was announced on 14 August (Shimura, Thm 2.20).
name: The valence formula at general level

about: for a Dedekind domain with fraction field K and a set S of primes, 1 → 𝒪_S^×/(𝒪_S^×)ⁿ → K(S, n) → Cl_S[n] → 1 is exact, so K(S, n) is finite when Cl_S is finite and 𝒪_S^× is finitely generated, in particular for a number field and finite S — the three TODOs of Mathlib's `SelmerGroup.lean`; extended to finite étale algebras in TauCeti#4610 (Silverman, AEC VIII.1).
name: The Selmer group K(S, n) is finite, via its fundamental exact sequence

about: the Atkin–Lehner anti-involution fixes every double coset Γ₀(N)xΓ₀(N), x ∈ Δ₀(N), so Shimura's criterion of 4 August makes R(Γ₀(N), Δ₀(N)) commutative, and the composite T_n = ∏_p T_{p^{v_p(n)}} satisfies T_{mn} = T_m T_n for coprime m, n (TauCeti#4720); the abstract Hecke ring is being upstreamed (mathlib4#41251, mathlib4#41277) (Shimura §3.3).
name: The Hecke ring of Γ₀(N) is commutative

about: for E: y² = f(x) over a field of characteristic ≠ 2, the map μ : E(K) → A^×/(A^×)² announced yesterday has kernel exactly 2E(K), so E(K)/2E(K) embeds in the square classes of A = K[X]/(f) — the injectivity half of 2-descent (Silverman, AEC X.1).
name: The kernel of the x − T map is 2E(K)

about: for a Dedekind domain A and any finite extension L of its fraction field, the integral closure of A in L is Dedekind; Mathlib has this for separable L/K, and the Krull–Akizuki theorem of 25 August removes the separability, which now covers inseparable isogenies of elliptic curves (Bourbaki, *Commutative Algebra*, VII §2.5).
name: The integral closure of a Dedekind domain is Dedekind, with no separability

about: for a mixed Hodge structure the subspaces I^{p,q} of 24 August are independent and span the complexification, with (W_k)_ℂ = ⊕_{p+q ≤ k} I^{p,q}; recovery of F and the conjugation symmetry remain (Deligne, *Théorie de Hodge II*, 1.2.8).
name: Deligne's bigrading is an internal direct sum

about: Ind_B^{GL₂}(α ⊗ β) is irreducible if and only if α ≠ β; and the Steinberg character takes the values q, 1, 0, −1 on central, split semisimple, non-semisimple and elliptic elements (TauCeti#4732) (Fulton–Harris §5.2).
name: The principal series of GL₂(𝔽_q) is irreducible exactly off the diagonal

about: for a polarised quadratic space of dimension 2l + 1 over a separably closed field of characteristic ≠ 2, the even Clifford algebra is all of End(⋀W), so the spin representation is irreducible — the type B companion of the half-spin dichotomy of 21 August (Fulton–Harris §20.2).
name: The spin representation is irreducible in odd dimension

about: for a Markov kernel on a countable state space and a state a₀ returned to infinitely often almost surely, the successive excursions from a₀ are i.i.d., and the chain is the image of the infinite product of the excursion law under concatenation (Norris, *Markov Chains*, Ch. 1).
name: The excursions of a recurrent Markov chain are i.i.d.

about: a C¹ vector field on a boundaryless manifold has through each point a maximal integral curve on an open interval, and at a finite endpoint the curve has no cluster point, so it leaves every compact set; hence every C¹ field on a compact manifold is complete (Lee, *Introduction to Smooth Manifolds*, 9.16, 9.19).
name: Maximal integral curves and the escape lemma

about: R(G), the split Grothendieck ring of FDRep k G under ⊕ and ⊗, with the character homomorphism R(G) → (G → k) whose image is exactly the virtual characters; injectivity is a later step (Serre, §9.1).
name: The representation ring

about: ω = dx/(2y + a₁x + a₃) in the Kähler differentials Ω_{K(E)/F} of the function field, with ω ≠ 0 in every characteristic; that div ω = 0 is not yet proved (Silverman, AEC III.1).
name: The invariant differential of an elliptic curve

about: for an elliptic curve y² = x³ + a₂x² + a₄x + a₆ over the fraction field K of a Dedekind domain in characteristic ≠ 2, the subgroup 2E(K) has finite index in E(K), provided that for each irreducible factor p of the cubic the ring of integers of K[X]/(p) has finite class group and finitely generated unit group, as it does over a number field; proved by explicit 2-descent through the étale algebra K[X]/(f), adapting Michael Stoll's Lean development, and it is the finiteness that the descent argument for the Mordell–Weil theorem itself consumes (Silverman, AEC VIII.1).
name: The weak Mordell–Weil theorem

about: for 1 ≤ p < ∞, on a proper normed abelian group with Haar measure and with values in a finite-dimensional real space, a family of Lᵖ functions that is bounded in Lᵖ, has translation increments ‖f(· + h) − f‖ₚ uniformly small as h → 0, and is uniformly tight is totally bounded, hence relatively compact; proved through Arzelà–Ascoli applied to ball averages, and it is the input Rellich–Kondrachov needs (Brezis, Thm 4.26).
name: The Fréchet–Kolmogorov compactness criterion in Lᵖ

about: every analytic subset of a Polish space is measurable for the completion of every s-finite Borel measure (Lusin; Kechris, Classical Descriptive Set Theory, Thm 21.10), and hence the strict sublevel sets of a Borel c-transform in optimal transport are analytic, which makes c-transforms measurable in every finite-measure completion.
name: Analytic sets are universally measurable

about: for a function field F/k with exact constant field, a proper subset S of its places, finitely many P₁, …, Pᵣ ∈ S, targets fᵢ ∈ F and integers rᵢ, a single x ∈ F has ord(x − fᵢ) = rᵢ at every Pᵢ and is regular at every other place of S (Stichtenoth, Thm 1.6.5); proved from Riemann's theorem through the repartition space, in the form Goppa-code applications use.
name: Strong approximation for algebraic function fields

about: for any topological group G, normal subgroup N and topological G-module M, the sequence 0 → H¹(G/N, Mᴺ) → H¹(G, M) → H¹(N, M) of explicit continuous-cochain cohomology is exact (Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg (1.6.7)); Mathlib has the discrete-group version for Rep k G.
name: The inflation–restriction exact sequence for continuous cohomology

about: for a profinite group G, a closed subgroup U and a discrete U-module A, evaluation at 1 induces H⁰(G, Coindᴳ A) ≅ H⁰(U, A) and H¹(G, Coindᴳ A) ≅ H¹(U, A), the inverse built from a continuous section of G → G/U (Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg (1.6.4)); degree 2 is not yet covered, and Mathlib has the discrete-group statement.
name: Shapiro's lemma for continuous cohomology in degrees 0 and 1

about: two smooth homomorphisms out of a preconnected finite-dimensional real Lie group that induce the same map of Lie algebras are equal, by naturality of the exponential map and its local inverse near the identity (Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, Ch. 20).
name: Faithfulness of the Lie functor on connected Lie groups

about: for F/k with exact constant field, the Weil differentials Ω (the k-linear forms on the repartition space vanishing on some A(D) + F, with F acting by (f·ω)(a) = ω(f a)) satisfy dim_k Ω(D) = i(D), the index of specialty, and dim_F Ω = 1 (Stichtenoth, Lemma 1.5.7 and Prop. 1.5.9); the canonical divisor, duality and Riemann–Roch itself are the remaining steps.
name: The Weil differentials of a function field form a one-dimensional space over it

about: if x is a separating element of F/k (x transcendental over k and F separable over k(x)), then Ω[F/k] is a one-dimensional F-vector space with basis dx, and y ↦ dy/dx is a k-derivation of F with dy = (dy/dx)·dx (Stichtenoth §IV.1), obtained from formally étale base change of Kähler differentials along k(x) → F.
name: The Kähler differentials of a function field are one-dimensional

about: for Ãₙ, D̃ₙ, Ẽ₆, Ẽ₇, Ẽ₈ the symmetrized Cartan form is positive semidefinite and its radical is exactly the line ℝδ spanned by the marks (Kac, Infinite-Dimensional Lie Algebras, Ch. 4), and deleting the affine node leaves the finite Cartan matrix of type Aₙ, Dₙ, E₆, E₇, E₈ in Bourbaki's numbering.
name: The affine simply-laced Cartan form is positive semidefinite with radical spanned by the marks

about: in the Fock model ⋀W of a polarisation V = W ⊕ W' ⊕ L, the commuting Clifford bivectors ½(wᵢw'ᵢ − w'ᵢwᵢ) act diagonally with weights exactly the 2ˡ half-integer sign vectors ½(±1, …, ±1), each weight space a line (Fulton–Harris §20.1); the comparison with the abstract Bₗ and Dₗ root data is still to come.
name: The weights of the spin representation

about: restriction to a Dedekind model R ⊂ F is a surjection Cl(F) → ClassGroup R whose kernel is generated by the classes of the places at infinity, and when R has a single place at infinity and it is rational this restricts to Cl⁰(F) ≅ ClassGroup R (Hartshorne II 6.5); it is the general form of the elliptic-curve case announced earlier, E(K) ≅ ClassGroup of the coordinate ring.
name: The degree-zero class group of a function field is the class group of an affine model

about: on an integral Noetherian scheme regular in codimension one, the subsheaf of the sheaf of rational functions whose sections over U are the f with ord(f) ≥ −D(x) at every codimension-one point x ∈ U (Hartshorne II §6); D ≤ E gives 𝒪(D) → 𝒪(E), multiplication by g is an isomorphism 𝒪(D) ≅ 𝒪(D − div g), so linearly equivalent divisors have isomorphic sheaves; invertibility for locally principal D is the next step.
name: The sheaf 𝒪(D) of a Weil divisor

about: the holomorphy ring ⋂ 𝒪ₚ over a set S of places is integrally closed in F, every k-subalgebra of F integrally closed in F is the holomorphy ring of the places at which its elements are regular, and S is recovered from its holomorphy ring (Stichtenoth, Thm 3.2.6 and Cor. 3.2.8).
name: Integrally closed subalgebras of a function field are holomorphy rings

about: for an elliptic curve E over a number field K the group E(K) of K-rational points is finitely generated, and its torsion subgroup is finite; the descent runs from the weak theorem (TauCeti#4857) and the naive x-coordinate height with its approximate parallelogram law |h(P+Q) + h(P−Q) − 2h(P) − 2h(Q)| ≤ C and Northcott property (TauCeti#4882), with no canonical height involved (Silverman, AEC VIII.4).
name: The Mordell–Weil theorem

about: Cl(p, q) is isomorphic over ℝ to a matrix algebra over ℝ, ℂ or ℍ, or to a product of two matrix algebras over ℝ or over ℍ, according to (q − p) mod 8 and with the matrix sizes explicit, and the eightfold periodicity Cl(p+8, q) ≅ Cl(p, q) ⊗ M₁₆(ℝ) holds for every signature (Lawson–Michelsohn, Spin Geometry, Ch. I).
name: The classification of real Clifford algebras

about: on compact metrizable spaces, for a lower semicontinuous cost c : X × Y → [0, ∞] the minimal transport cost inf_π ∫ c dπ over couplings of μ and ν equals the supremum of ∫ φ dμ + ∫ ψ dν over continuous φ, ψ with φ(x) + ψ(y) ≤ c(x, y), both sides allowed to be ∞; this extends the continuous-cost duality of TauCeti#4494 by monotone approximation (Villani, Topics in Optimal Transportation, Thm 1.3).
name: Kantorovich duality for lower semicontinuous costs

about: for a bounded open Ω in a finite-dimensional real inner product space and 1 ≤ p < ∞, the inclusion W^{1,p}_0(Ω) → L^p(Ω) is a compact operator, with no regularity of ∂Ω assumed; the W^{1,p}(Ω) case under a Lipschitz boundary is a separate later milestone (Brezis, Cor. 9.16; Evans §5.7).
name: The Rellich–Kondrachov theorem on W^{1,p}_0(Ω)

about: for u ∈ W^{1,p}_0(Ω) and 1/p⋆ = 1/p − 1/n, ‖u‖_{L^{p⋆}(Ω)} ≤ C ‖∇u‖_{L^p} with Mathlib's explicit constant, giving the bounded embedding W^{1,p}_0(Ω) ↪ L^{p⋆}(Ω); Mathlib has the inequality for compactly supported C¹ functions, and the new content is the passage to their closure (Evans §5.6).
name: The Gagliardo–Nirenberg–Sobolev inequality on W^{1,p}_0(Ω)

about: a flasque sheaf of abelian groups on a topological space has Hⁿ(U, F) = 0 for every n ≥ 1 and every open U; injective abelian sheaves and skyscraper sheaves are flasque, hence acyclic, by the classical dimension shift run through Mathlib's Ext-based sheaf cohomology (Hartshorne III.2; Godement).
name: Flasque sheaves are acyclic

about: for squarefree d ∉ ℚ², the compositum of the fields ℚ(√P) over the prime discriminants P dividing the fundamental discriminant of d is abelian over ℚ, unramified over ℚ(√d) at every finite place, and contains every abelian extension of ℚ with those two properties, so any such extension has degree at most 2^t for t the number of ramified primes and is isomorphic to the compositum when the bound is attained; the infinite places are unconstrained, hence "narrow" (Cox, Primes of the Form x² + ny², §6.A; Lemmermeyer, Reciprocity Laws, §2.2).
name: The narrow genus field of a quadratic field

about: for an algebraic function field F/k with k finite, Cl⁰(F) is finite, which defines the class number h_F = #Cl⁰(F); the proof counts places and effective divisors of bounded degree and uses Riemann's inequality, and Mathlib's `FunctionField.classNumber`, the class group of the ring of integers of one affine chart, is a different group whose comparison with Cl⁰(F) is a later step (Stichtenoth, Algebraic Function Fields and Codes, §5.1).
name: The degree-zero divisor class group of a global function field is finite

about: for a finite extension F'/F of function fields generated by y and a place P of F, the monic irreducible factors of the minimal polynomial of y reduced modulo P give distinct places over P whose relative degrees are at least the factors' degrees (TauCeti#4921), and when the prime of an affine model R is prime to the conductor of R[y] these are all the places over P, with residue degree the factor's degree and ramification index its multiplicity; the Dedekind-domain half generalises Mathlib's number-field Kummer–Dedekind computation of e and f to arbitrary Dedekind domains (Stichtenoth Thm 3.3.7, Cor 3.3.8).
name: Kummer's theorem for the places of a function field

about: s_μ = Σ_ν K_{μν} m_ν in finitely many variables, writing a Schur polynomial in the monomial symmetric polynomials with the Kostka numbers of TauCeti#1684 as coefficients; that the two families are bases of the symmetric polynomials is not claimed (Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, I.6; Stanley, EC2 §7.10).
name: The Kostka expansion of Schur polynomials

about: a Tits system (BN-pair) is defined by subgroups B, N generating G with B ∩ N normal in N and simple reflections generating W = N/(B ∩ N) subject to BsB · BwB ⊆ BswB ∪ BwB and sBs⁻¹ ≠ B, and for every Tits system the double cosets BnB, n ∈ N, cover G, so N → B\G/B is surjective; GL₂(k) with its upper triangular subgroup and the normalizer of the diagonal torus is an instance (TauCeti#5005), and that distinct elements of W give distinct cells is not yet proved (Bourbaki, Lie IV §2; Humphreys, Linear Algebraic Groups, §28.1).
name: Tits systems and their Bruhat cells

about: for an affine group scheme G of finite type over a field, R_u(G) is constructed as the greatest connected normal smooth unipotent closed subgroup, characterised by the universal property of its defining Hopf ideal and invariant under isomorphism (TauCeti#5039), and G is reductive exactly when it is smooth and geometrically connected with R_u(G ×_k k̄) trivial (Milne, Algebraic Groups, 6.42–6.46; Borel, Linear Algebraic Groups, §11.21).
name: The unipotent radical

about: f ↦ f ∣ₖ W with W = [[0, −1], [N, 0]], as a ℂ-linear endomorphism of M_k(Γ₁(N)) and of S_k(Γ₁(N)) (TauCeti#4455), which squares to the nonzero scalar (−1)^k N^{k−2} and so is an automorphism (TauCeti#4484), and which shifts the diamond operators by W ∘ ⟨d⟩ = ⟨d⁻¹⟩ ∘ W; this is the un-normalised operator, the normalised involution and the Atkin–Lehner operators W_Q being later rungs (Miyake, Modular Forms, §4.6).
name: The Fricke operator

about: f is a Stieltjes function when f(t) = a/t + b + ∫₀^∞ (t + x)⁻¹ dμ(x) on (0, ∞) with a, b ≥ 0 and μ a measure on [0, ∞) with ∫ (1 + x)⁻¹ dμ < ∞; they form a convex cone (TauCeti#4957), and every Stieltjes function is completely monotone on (0, ∞), with dⁿ/dtⁿ ∫ (t + x)⁻¹ dμ = (−1)ⁿ n! ∫ (t + x)^{−n−1} dμ (Schilling–Song–Vondraček, Bernstein Functions, Thm 2.2).
name: Stieltjes functions

about: for every Young diagram μ with n cells, the number f^μ of standard Young tableaux of shape μ satisfies f^μ · ∏_{c ∈ μ} h(c) = n!, proved by the Frame–Robinson–Thrall route through the beta-numbers βᵢ = λᵢ + r − 1 − i and the Frobenius determinant formula f^μ · ∏ᵢ βᵢ! = n! · ∏_{i<j} (βᵢ − βⱼ) (Macdonald I.1 Ex. 1, Sagan §3.10).
name: The hook-length formula

about: on (kⁿ)^{⊗d} over a field with d! ≠ 0, the image of k[S_d] permuting the tensor factors and the span of the diagonal operators f^{⊗d}, f ranging over all endomorphisms of kⁿ, are each other's commutants; that the invertible g^{⊗d} alone already span, and hence the statement for the image of k[GLₙ], is not yet proved (Fulton–Harris Lecture 6, Procesi Ch. 9).
name: Schur–Weyl duality, the double centralizer

about: if two bounded closed sets S, T ⊆ ℂ have preconnected intersection and neither separates a from b, then S ∪ T does not separate them either; it is read off Borsuk's criterion, that a and b lie in one component of Kᶜ exactly when (z − a)/(z − b) has a continuous logarithm on the bounded closed set K, the input the Carathéodory boundary correspondence for Jordan domains is waiting on (Burckel §4, Munkres §§61–63).
name: Janiszewski's theorem

about: for a bounded coercive divergence-form energy form B on H¹₀(Ω) with Ω bounded and any real κ, the weak problem B(u, v) − κ⟨u, v⟩_{L²} = ⟨f, v⟩_{L²} either has a nonzero homogeneous solution or has a unique solution for every f ∈ L²(Ω), the homogeneous solution space being finite-dimensional, via Rellich–Kondrachov and the abstract Fredholm alternative for compact operators (Evans §6.2.3, Gilbarg–Trudinger Thm 8.3).
name: The Fredholm alternative for the Dirichlet problem

about: the generator A of a strongly continuous unitary group on a complex Hilbert space is skew-adjoint, A† = −A, on its natural domain; strongly continuous one-parameter groups on Banach spaces are set up alongside (TauCeti#5154), with two-sided growth bounds, orbits differentiable on all of ℝ and uniqueness of the group given its generator, while the converse construction of e^{itH} from a self-adjoint H is not yet done (Reed–Simon Thm VIII.8).
name: Stone's theorem, the generator direction

about: over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, every nonzero finite-dimensional 𝔤𝔩ₙ-module has a highest weight vector for the matrix-unit positive system and its weight is dominant integral (TauCeti#5150), two irreducibles with highest weight vectors of the same weight are isomorphic, and every weakly decreasing tuple of naturals is realised as a highest weight in an exterior power of the standard module (TauCeti#5169); the named irreducible for each dominant weight is still to come (Humphreys §20, Fulton–Harris §15).
name: The highest weight theorem for 𝔤𝔩ₙ

about: the number of Gelfand–Tsetlin patterns with top row λ equals the Weyl product ∏_{i<j} (λᵢ − λⱼ + j − i)/(j − i), proved from the branching recursion and a box-sum identity for integer Vandermonde determinants; this is an identity between a lattice-point count and a product, with no representation of GLₙ attached to either side yet (Fulton–Harris §15.3).
name: The Gelfand–Tsetlin dimension formula

about: the explicit full-weight Chevalley–Demazure carrier of type A_r built from the Kostant ℤ-form has points SL_{r+1}(K) over every field K, generated by its root subgroups, and the fixed points of its q-power Frobenius are SL_{r+1}(𝔽) for 𝔽 the fixed subfield, a finite group SL_{r+1}(q) in characteristic p (TauCeti#5193): the first finite group of Lie type the construction produces (Steinberg, *Lectures on Chevalley Groups*, §§3–4).
name: The type-A Chevalley–Demazure group is SL_{r+1}

about: for a finite separable extension F'/F of algebraic function fields and a place P of F, the integral closure of 𝒪_P in F' is free of rank [F' : F] over 𝒪_P with a basis that is an F-basis of F' (TauCeti#5118), and any fixed F-basis of F' is an integral basis at all but finitely many places (Stichtenoth Cor. 3.3.5, Thm 3.3.6).
name: Local integral bases of function fields

about: the Chevalley generators of E₆ and E₇ realised as integer matrices on the minuscule weight orbits, with the Chevalley–Serre relations verified over ℤ and, for E₆, the coordinate lattice stable under the Kostant divided-power form (TauCeti#5204); no identification with the abstract irreducible highest-weight modules is claimed (Bourbaki Plates V–VI, Humphreys §13.4).
name: The 27- and 56-dimensional minuscule representations of E₆ and E₇

about: for a trivial-intersection subgroup H of a finite group G, the Frobenius kernel {1} ∪ (G ∖ ⋃ gHg⁻¹) is a normal subgroup and a complement to H, so G = N ⋊ H; closure of the kernel under multiplication is proved by Frobenius's character-theoretic argument, for which no character-free proof is known (Isaacs, *Character Theory of Finite Groups*, Ch. 7).
name: Frobenius's theorem

about: every finite-dimensional irreducible continuous representation of SU(2) is equivalent to the symmetric power Symᵈ(ℂ²) for exactly one d, with unitarity discharged by the unitarian trick rather than assumed; the analytic input is the Chebyshev identity χ_d = U_d(tr/2) and the uniform density of the character span in the continuous class functions (TauCeti#5282) (Bröcker–tom Dieck, *Representations of Compact Lie Groups*, II.4–5).
name: The irreducible representations of SU(2), classified

about: ∏_{α>0}(1 − e^{−α}) = Σ_{w∈W} sgn(w) e^{w(ρ)−ρ} in the integral group algebra of the weight lattice of a finite crystallographic root system, proved combinatorially for an abstract root pairing with no Lie algebra entering; it is the denominator half of the Weyl character formula, whose Verma-character half is still to come (Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*, §24).
name: The Weyl denominator identity

about: for a partition μ with at most n rows the Weyl dimension ∏_{i<j}(λᵢ − λⱼ + j − i)/(j − i) equals ∏_{(i,j)∈μ}(n + j − i)/h(i,j), each cell contributing n plus its content over its hook length, stated division-free over ℕ; identifying this number with the dimension of an irreducible GLₙ representation is a separate later step (Fulton–Harris, *Representation Theory*, Thm 6.3).
name: The hook-content formula

about: over any commutative ring, the polynomials in m variables that are symmetric and homogeneous of degree n form a free module with the Schur polynomials, indexed by the partitions of n into at most m parts, as a basis, the change of basis from the monomial symmetric polynomials being the unitriangular Kostka matrix (Macdonald, *Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials*, I.6).
name: The Schur polynomials are a basis

about: a morphism of mixed Hodge structures is strict for both filtrations, im f ∩ W′ₖ = f(Wₖ) and im f ∩ F′ᵖ = f(Fᵖ), proved by recovering the Hodge filtration from Deligne's bigrading; this is the theorem behind the abelian-ness of the category of mixed Hodge structures, a packaging still to come (Deligne, *Théorie de Hodge II*; Peters–Steenbrink, *Mixed Hodge Structures*).
name: Strictness of morphisms of mixed Hodge structures

about: for a Garnir set X straddling two adjacent columns of a Young tableau t, the signed sum Σ_σ sgn(σ)σ over the permutations of X annihilates the polytabloid e_t; these are the relations that straighten arbitrary polytabloids, and the standard basis of the Specht module built on them is a later step (James, *The Representation Theory of the Symmetric Groups*, §7).
name: The Garnir relations

about: χ²ₖ for real k ≥ 0, with density, cdf P(k/2, x/2), mean k, variance 2k, mgf (1 − 2t)^(−k/2), characteristic function (1 − 2it)^(−k/2), and additivity of degrees of freedom under convolution; the characteristic function of the gamma distribution is proved along the way, by analytic continuation of the moment generating function.
name: The chi-squared distribution

about: the rank-n invariant-subspace form of the unreduced Burau representation of TauCeti#4218, now carved out explicitly with the two-strand normalization σ₀ ↦ −t; this is the representation the braid-closure algorithm for the Alexander polynomial runs on (Birman, *Braids, Links, and Mapping Class Groups*, Ch. 3).
name: The reduced Burau representation

about: Tr M, the cokernel of the dual of a projective presentation P₁ → P₀ → M → 0, shown independent of the chosen minimal presentation and vanishing on projectives; the construction from which the Auslander–Reiten translate τ = D Tr and AR duality will be formed (Auslander–Reiten–Smalø, *Representation Theory of Artin Algebras*, IV.1).
name: The Auslander–Reiten transpose

about: R(G) for a finite-type affine group scheme, the greatest connected normal smooth closed subgroup with geometrically solvable points, with its universal property, the containment of the unipotent radical, and the characterization of semisimplicity as triviality of R(G) after base change to an algebraic closure (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, 6.42–6.46).
name: The solvable radical

about: every graphon is within ε in cut norm of its block average over a measurable partition with at most 4^(⌈1/ε²⌉+1) parts (Frieze–Kannan 1999; Lovász, *Large Networks and Graph Limits*, §9.2) — the exponential bound that trades Szemerédi's tower for a weaker approximation.
name: Frieze–Kannan weak regularity

about: over a quiver with positive definite Tits form, a finite-dimensional indecomposable representation is determined up to isomorphism by its dimension vector, by the Bernstein–Gelfand–Ponomarev reflection induction; the existence half, that every positive root is so realized, is separate later work.
name: The uniqueness half of Gabriel's theorem

about: on a finite-dimensional highest weight module of weight λ over a Killing-semisimple Lie algebra, (⟨λ+ρ, λ+ρ⟩ − ⟨μ+ρ, μ+ρ⟩)·dim M_μ = 2 Σ_{α>0} Σ_{j≥1} dim M_{μ+jα}·⟨μ+jα, α⟩ (Humphreys, GTM 9, §22.3), and the left coefficient is nonzero for μ ≠ λ, so the recursion computes every weight multiplicity downward from dim M_λ = 1.
name: Freudenthal's multiplicity formula

about: the triangle density of a graphon is at least 2d² − d in its edge density d (Goodman 1959), whence Mantel's bound: a graphon with zero triangle density has edge density at most 1/2.
name: Goodman's inequality for graphons

about: over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, two finite-dimensional representations of a finite group with equal characters are isomorphic, and the character map on the representation ring R(G) is injective (Serre, *Linear Representations of Finite Groups*, §2.3); Mathlib has the forward direction and the orthogonality relations, and this is the converse.
name: Finite-group representations are determined by their characters

about: the integral closure of k[X₁, …, Xᵣ] in a finite purely inseparable extension of its fraction field is a finite module (Stacks 032O); Mathlib's finiteness theorem argues through the trace pairing and so covers the separable case, and this is the inseparable half of normalization finiteness.
name: Integral closure in a purely inseparable extension is finite

about: Σ_{T ⊆ Φ⁺} (−1)^|T| P(ν − Σ_{α∈T} α) = δ_{ν,0}, the coefficientwise form of Δ · Σ_ν P(ν) e^{−ν} = 1 (Kostant 1959), the combinatorial input to the Kostant multiplicity and Weyl character formulas.
name: The Kostant partition function inverts the Weyl denominator

about: for ζ an m-th root of unity in an extension of a number field and 𝔭 a prime of the base not dividing m, every arithmetic Frobenius at a prime above 𝔭 sends ζ to ζ^𝔑𝔭 (Washington, *Introduction to Cyclotomic Fields*, Ch. 1), so the mod-m cyclotomic character reads Frob_p ↦ p mod m.
name: An arithmetic Frobenius raises roots of unity to the norm of the prime below

about: for a cusp form f ∈ S_k(Γ₁(N), χ) and squarefree L whose primes all divide N, some cusp form of level LN has the q-expansion of f restricted to the indices coprime to L (Miyake, *Modular Forms*, Lemma 4.6.5), the root of the descent tower toward strong multiplicity one.
name: Miyake's coprime-index filter

about: the measure with density Γ((ν+1)/2)/(√(νπ) Γ(ν/2)) · (1 + x²/ν)^(−(ν+1)/2), proved a probability measure via Euler's second beta integral ∫₀^∞ x^(a−1)(1+x)^(−a−b) dx = Β(a,b), itself new here, with one degree of freedom recovering the Cauchy law.
name: Student's t distribution

about: the conjugacy-class-valued Frobenius of a prime of a number field unramified in a finite Galois extension, well defined because every arithmetic Frobenius at every prime above it represents the same class (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, I §9); it packages Mathlib's arithmetic-Frobenius theory into the symbol the Chebotarev density theorem is stated with.
name: The Artin symbol of an unramified prime

about: the algebra homomorphism χ_λ : Z(U(L)) → K by which the centre of the enveloping algebra acts on every highest weight vector of weight λ — the infinitesimal character (Humphreys, *BGG Category O*, §1.7) — taking the Casimir element to its eigenvalue; the Harish-Chandra isomorphism is separate later work.
name: The central character of a highest weight module

about: for every dominant integral weight μ over a field of characteristic zero there is a finite-dimensional irreducible 𝔤𝔩ₙ-module L(μ) with highest weight μ, constructed as the irreducible quotient of the submodule generated by a realizing highest weight vector and identified with any irreducible carrying such a vector, and restriction to 𝔰𝔩ₙ stays irreducible over any characteristic-zero field since the identity matrix acts by Σᵢ μᵢ — the existence half that the highest weight theorem for 𝔤𝔩ₙ of TauCeti#5155 was still waiting on, completing the classification (Goodman–Wallach, GTM 255, §5.5).
name: The irreducible 𝔤𝔩ₙ-module of a dominant weight

about: K₀ modulo the radical of the Euler form: for two extension-closed subcategories on which the pairing χ(X, Y) = Σᵢ (−1)ⁱ dim Extⁱ(X, Y) is defined, it descends from the exact Grothendieck groups to left and right numerical quotients on which it is nondegenerate, computed on object classes by the Euler characteristic itself — the abstract form of the numerical Grothendieck group of Bridgeland, Ann. of Math. 166 (2007), §1.3.
name: The numerical Grothendieck quotients of the Ext-Euler pairing

about: a valuation is microbial when some convex subgroup of its value group has height-one quotient; rank-one valuations are microbial and trivial ones are not (Wedhorn, *Adic Spaces*, Def. 5.46(v)) — the condition through which analytic points of Spa(A, A⁺) acquire the height-one vertical generizations consumed by Wedhorn's Proposition 7.49(2).
name: Microbial valuations

about: a finite-dimensional division algebra with centre ℝ is ℝ-isomorphic to ℝ or to Hamilton's quaternions ℍ, whence every real Brauer class is trivial or the class of ℍ and the Brauer group of ℝ is ℤ/2 (Gille–Szamuely, *Central Simple Algebras and Galois Cohomology*).
name: Frobenius' theorem on real division algebras

about: π₁(ℝPⁿ) is trivial for n = 0, infinite for n = 1 (ℝP¹ is a circle), and of order two for every n ≥ 2 via the double cover Sⁿ → ℝPⁿ, now assembled as one trichotomy covering all dimensions (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, §1.3).
name: Fundamental groups of real projective spaces

about: the finiteness half of Gabriel's theorem: a finite quiver whose Tits form is positive definite has only finitely many indecomposable finite-dimensional representations up to isomorphism, at most one per positive root, composing the dimension-vector facts behind the uniqueness half of TauCeti#5299; the existence half and the ADE classification remain (Gabriel, *Unzerlegbare Darstellungen I*, 1972).
name: A positive definite Tits form forces finite representation type

about: two triplets of killing coefficient, nonnegative drift, and Lévy measure representing the same Bernstein function on [0, ∞) coincide, upgrading the existence theorem of TauCeti#4483 to unique existence and completing the representation theorem (Schilling–Song–Vondraček, *Bernstein Functions*, Thm 3.2).
name: Uniqueness in the Lévy–Khintchine representation of Bernstein functions

about: for l ∣ N and a Dirichlet character χ mod N, a periodic f : ℍ → ℂ whose rescaling f(l·) is a cusp form in S_k(N, χ) either has χ factoring through N/l with f itself a cusp form of level N/l and the lowered character, or is zero (Miyake, *Modular Forms*, Thm 4.6.4); ported clause-for-clause from Chris Birkbeck's AINTLIB.
name: The level-lowering dichotomy for cusp forms

about: the infimum over couplings π of μ and ν of the L^p-norm of the ground distance under π, with p = ∞ a case of the same definition; symmetry, the triangle inequality by gluing plus Minkowski, monotonicity in the exponent, and separation of probability measures on a Polish space are proved, opening the metric layer of the optimal-transport development (Villani, *Optimal Transport*, Ch. 6).
name: The p-Wasserstein distance

about: formal products ∏ p^(e_p) with exponents in ℕ ∪ {∞}, carrying the divisibility complete lattice, primary decompositions, and the embedding of the positive naturals: the arithmetic in which orders and indices of profinite groups are counted (Ribes–Zalesskii, *Profinite Groups*, §2.3).
name: Supernatural numbers

about: a square-zero degree-one endomorphism of an internally ℤ-graded algebra obeying the graded Leibniz rule, with cycles a graded subalgebra, boundaries a homogeneous two-sided ideal, and the graded cohomology algebra as the quotient — the opening layer of the DG/A∞ development (Weibel, *An Introduction to Homological Algebra*).
name: Differential graded algebras

about: τ M = D(Tr M), the k-dual of the transpose of TauCeti#5217, proved independent of the chosen minimal projective presentation and vanishing on projectives; AR duality and the bijection between non-projective and non-injective indecomposables are still to come (Auslander–Reiten–Smalø, *Representation Theory of Artin Algebras*, IV).
name: The Auslander–Reiten translate

about: the Riemann map of a Jordan domain extends to a homeomorphism of the closed disc onto the closure of the domain, proved through cluster sets and Janiszewski's separation theorem rather than the Schoenflies theorem (Pommerenke, *Boundary Behaviour of Conformal Maps*, Ch. 2).
name: Carathéodory's boundary extension theorem

about: ĥ(P) = lim 4⁻ⁿ h(2ⁿP)/2 on an elliptic curve, by Tate's telescoping limit, with bounded difference from the naïve height, the exact parallelogram law, ĥ(nP) = n²ĥ(P), ĥ ≥ 0, and — under Northcott finiteness — ĥ(P) = 0 exactly at the torsion points; the Néron–Tate pairing and regulator are the next milestones (Silverman, *AEC*, VIII §9).
name: The canonical Néron–Tate height

about: ζ_K(s) = ∏ (1 − N𝔭⁻ˢ)⁻¹ over the primes of 𝓞_K for Re s > 1, from a general analytic Euler product for absolutely convergent ideal-indexed Dirichlet series; the prime-ideal counterpart of Mathlib's Euler product for ζ(s) (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, Ch. VII).
name: The Euler product of the Dedekind zeta function

about: the chord addition series of a Weierstrass curve satisfies F(F(t₁,t₂),t₃) = F(t₁,F(t₂,t₃)) over every commutative ring, the last axiom of the commutative formal group law of Ê; registering Ê as an instance of Mathlib's abstract formal groups is a separate later step (Silverman, *AEC*, IV §1).
name: Associativity of the elliptic formal group law

about: the map K₀(proj R) → G₀(mod R) of Grothendieck groups is an isomorphism whenever every finitely generated R-module admits a finite resolution by finitely generated projectives, e.g. over a semisimple ring (Weibel, *The K-book*, II §6.2 and V §3).
name: The Cartan map and the resolution theorem

about: a Poisson law whose intensity is itself Gamma-distributed is a negative binomial law (Johnson–Kemp–Kotz, *Univariate Discrete Distributions*, Ch. 6).
name: The Gamma–Poisson mixture is negative binomial

about: the sum of squares of a finite independent family of standard Gaussian variables has the χ² law with that many degrees of freedom (Johnson–Kotz–Balakrishnan, *Continuous Univariate Distributions*, vol. 1).
name: Squares of Gaussians are chi-squared

about: a Borel subgroup of a linear algebraic group scheme, in Hopf coordinates: a smooth, geometrically connected, geometrically solvable closed subgroup maximal among such, with the upper-triangular subgroup of GL₂ proved Borel over every field via Bruhat decomposition (Springer, *Linear Algebraic Groups*, §6.2).
name: Borel subgroups

about: the sequence 0 → τM → E → M → 0 as a short exact complex whose two maps are left and right almost split, with non-splitness, indecomposability of the ends and self-duality derived rather than assumed; the Auslander–Reiten existence theorem is a later target (Auslander–Reiten–Smalø, *Representation Theory of Artin Algebras*, V.1).
name: Almost-split (Auslander–Reiten) sequences

about: the F(m,n) law as a pushforward of the Beta law, with cumulative distribution function the regularized incomplete beta function at mx/(n + mx); density and moments are still to come (Johnson–Kotz–Balakrishnan, *Continuous Univariate Distributions*, vol. 2).
name: Fisher's F distribution

about: for an irreducible complex character χ of a finite group and an element g whose conjugacy class has size coprime to the degree χ(1), either χ(g) = 0 or ‖χ(g)‖ = χ(1) — the arithmetic dichotomy behind Burnside's pᵃqᵇ theorem, whose remaining steps are separate (Isaacs, *Character Theory of Finite Groups*, Thm 3.8).
name: Burnside's vanishing theorem

about: for L u = −∂ⱼ(aⁱʲ ∂ᵢu) + bⁱ ∂ᵢu + c u with a coercive symmetric energy form on a bounded open Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ, the solution operator on L²(Ω) is compact and self-adjoint (Rellich–Kondrachov plus Lax–Milgram), every Dirichlet eigenvalue is positive with the explicit Poincaré lower bound for −Δ, eigenspaces are finite-dimensional, and the eigenfunctions span a dense subspace of L²(Ω); the ordered eigenvalue sequence and min–max are later steps (Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, §6.5).
name: The Dirichlet spectrum of a divergence-form elliptic operator

about: the canonical height ĥ polarises to the symmetric bilinear pairing ⟨P, Q⟩ = (ĥ(P+Q) − ĥ(P) − ĥ(Q))/2 on the points of an elliptic curve, with ⟨P, P⟩ = ĥ(P) and the torsion in its kernel, descending to the Mordell–Weil group modulo torsion, where it is positive definite under Northcott finiteness and has a Gram matrix in any basis — the input to the regulator, which is the next step (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, VIII §9).
name: The Néron–Tate pairing

about: a globally Lipschitz vector field on a Banach space has a unique solution through every point defined on all of ℝ, by one Picard iteration in a cosh-weighted function space, and the solutions assemble into a jointly continuous flow with the group law and two-sided exponential dependence on initial conditions, extending Mathlib's interval-local Picard–Lindelöf; the negative gradient flow of Morse theory is the intended consumer (Dieudonné, *Foundations of Modern Analysis*, Ch. X).
name: The flow of a globally Lipschitz vector field

about: the level set of a C^m Fredholm map between Banach spaces at a regular value carries a C^m manifold structure modelled on the kernel of the derivative, of dimension the Fredholm index — the moduli-space package of McDuff–Salamon, *J-holomorphic Curves and Symplectic Topology*, Appendix A.3, upgrading the implicit-function charts of the local normal form (TauCeti#3235) to a smooth atlas.
name: A regular level set of a Fredholm map is a manifold

about: in the double-coset Hecke ring of Γ₀(N), Tₘ · Tₙ = Σ_{d ∣ gcd(m,n)} d · S_d · T_{mn/d²} for all nonzero m and n, deduced from the per-prime table by an induction on the gcd (Shimura, *Introduction to the Arithmetic Theory of Automorphic Functions*, Thm 3.24(3)).
name: The Hecke multiplication table for Γ₀(N)

about: for a finite subgroup Φ of the points of a Weierstrass curve, the function-field extension F(W)/F(W)^Φ is Galois of degree #Φ with the translations as its full automorphism group — the field-theoretic input to the dual isogeny (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, III.4.10) — via Artin's fixed-field theorem proved for any finite automorphism group with no finite-dimensionality hypothesis on the ambient extension.
name: The Galois theory of translations on an elliptic function field

about: on a Polish metric space and for 1 ≤ p < ∞, the finitely supported probability laws are dense in the Wasserstein space P_p(X), and the N-point quantization error of a fixed law tends to zero (Villani, *Optimal Transport: Old and New*; Graf–Luschgy, *Foundations of Quantization for Probability Distributions*).
name: Finitely supported measures are dense in Wasserstein space

about: every module — with no finiteness hypothesis — over a semiprimary ring has a projective cover, the existence half joining the uniqueness announced with TauCeti#3266; semiperfect rings are defined alongside, with semiprimary rings semiperfect (Lam, *A First Course in Noncommutative Rings*, §23–24).
name: Projective covers exist over a semiprimary ring

about: the orbits of Gal(p) on the roots of a polynomial biject with its monic irreducible factors, a separable factor's degree counting the roots in its orbit; hence a separable polynomial of positive degree is irreducible exactly when the root action is transitive, sharpening Mathlib's irreducible-implies-transitive to an equivalence (Dummit–Foote, *Abstract Algebra*, Ch. 14).
name: Galois orbits are the irreducible factors

about: a compact symmetric operator on any Hilbert space has a Hilbert basis of eigenvectors, and applied to the solution operator of L u = −∂ⱼ(aⁱʲ ∂ᵢu) + bⁱ ∂ᵢu + c u on a bounded open Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ this gives L²(Ω) an orthonormal basis of Dirichlet eigenfunctions, with the solution expansion L⁻¹f = Σ κ⁻¹⟨eₖ, f⟩eₖ — upgrading the density of eigenfunctions announced with TauCeti#5632 (Reed–Simon, *Methods of Modern Mathematical Physics I*; Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, §6.5).
name: An orthonormal basis of Dirichlet eigenfunctions

about: for the same operators, κ₁ is the minimum of the Rayleigh quotient a(u, u)/‖u‖² over nonzero u ∈ H¹₀(Ω), ‖·‖ the L²(Ω) norm, equivalently the greatest constant in the Poincaré-type inequality C‖u‖² ≤ a(u, u), with the minimum attained via Rellich–Kondrachov (Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, §6.5).
name: The Rayleigh characterisation of the first Dirichlet eigenvalue

about: every pointed connected cover of (X, x₀) is the quotient of the universal cover by a unique subgroup of π₁(X, x₀), so the parametrisation is a bijection under which unpointed isomorphism is conjugacy and regularity is normality (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Thm 1.38) — the subgroup form of the classification, beside the monodromy equivalence of categories announced earlier.
name: Subgroups classify the pointed connected covers

about: ℂ ⊗ S^μ is simple, distinct shapes give non-isomorphic modules, and every simple object of FDRep ℂ Sₙ arises for exactly one partition of n, so the irreducible complex characters of Sₙ are exactly the χ^μ — carrying the rational classification announced earlier across the base change, by absolute irreducibility and flatness of intertwiner spaces (James–Kerber, *The Representation Theory of the Symmetric Group*).
name: The complex Specht modules classify the irreducible representations of Sₙ

about: on an elliptic curve over any field the isogeny [n] has degree n² for every nonzero integer n, via the division-polynomial computation that x ∘ [n] = Φₙ/ΨSqₙ has degree n² as a rational map — the multiplication-by-n half of the degree theory the Hasse bound consumes (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, III.6.4(a)).
name: The degree of multiplication by n is n²

about: every graphon W on a probability carrier satisfies t(C₄, W) ≥ t(K₂, W)⁴: the homomorphism density of the four-cycle is at least the fourth power of the edge density, the C₄ case of Sidorenko's conjecture, by the classical Cauchy–Schwarz argument (Lovász, *Large Networks and Graph Limits*).
name: Sidorenko's inequality for the 4-cycle

about: at a prime Q of a finite Galois extension of number fields, unramified over 𝔭 below, an arithmetic Frobenius induces the residue-field Frobenius, has order the inertia degree f(Q/𝔭), generates the decomposition group, and is conjugated along the fibre by the Galois action (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, I §9).
name: The Frobenius generates the decomposition group

about: for 1 ≤ p < ∞ the finite-moment Wasserstein space is separable when X is separable and complete when X is complete and separable, by the classical path-space gluing of near-optimal couplings, so P_p of a Polish space is Polish (Villani, *Optimal Transport: Old and New*, Thm 6.18).
name: The Wasserstein space P_p(X) is complete and separable

about: for x′ = v(x) with v of class C^(n+1) and globally Lipschitz, the solution is jointly C^(n+1) in initial condition and time near t = 0, packaged as a genuine local flow with the law Φ(x, t + s) = Φ(Φ(x, t), s) for a field smooth only near a point — the C^k dependence extending Mathlib's Lipschitz estimate, by a time rescaling that turns the initial condition into a parameter (Lang, *Differential and Riemannian Manifolds*).
name: Smooth dependence of an ODE solution on its initial condition

about: a finite-dimensional irreducible module of highest weight λ over a split semisimple Lie algebra carries a nonzero invariant bilinear form exactly when −(w₀ • λ) = λ for the longest Weyl element w₀, the dual being irreducible of highest weight −(w₀ • λ) (Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*, §21.6; Bourbaki, *Groupes et algèbres de Lie*, VIII §7.5).
name: The self-duality criterion for irreducible highest-weight modules

about: the absolute determinant of the Gram matrix of the Néron–Tate pairing on a basis of the points modulo torsion, independent of the chosen basis, with Reg = 1 at rank zero — completing the canonical-height strand the pairing (TauCeti#5660) opened; positivity awaits positive-definiteness on the real span (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, VIII §9).
name: The regulator of an elliptic curve

about: the vector field (x, v) ↦ (v, −Γₓ(v, v)) on the tangent bundle of a Riemannian manifold, whose integral curves are proved to be exactly the velocity lifts t ↦ (γ(t), γ′(t)) of geodesics — the object that feeds the exponential map and Hopf–Rinow, with smoothness of the spray itself the next step (do Carmo, *Riemannian Geometry*, Ch. 3).
name: The geodesic spray

about: a finite group of order pᵃqᵇ, for primes p and q, is solvable, by the classical character-theoretic route: a conjugacy class of prime-power size larger than one forces a proper nontrivial normal subgroup, which spends the vanishing theorem of TauCeti#5578, and an induction on the order with a Sylow argument finishes; this closes the milestone that bullet left open (Burnside 1904; Isaacs, *Character Theory of Finite Groups*, Thm 3.10).
name: Burnside's pᵃqᵇ theorem

about: a densely defined self-adjoint operator A on a complex Hilbert space is the generator of exactly one strongly continuous unitary group e^{itA}, and an operator is self-adjoint exactly when iA generates such a group; this is the converse direction that the generator bullet of TauCeti#5185 left open, obtained by gluing the Lumer–Phillips contraction semigroups of iA and −iA into a group (Reed–Simon, *Methods of Modern Mathematical Physics I*, Thm VIII.8; Engel–Nagel, Thm II.3.24).
name: Stone's theorem for unbounded self-adjoint operators

about: in an arbitrary Coxeter system, if a reflection t shortens w then t·w is spelled by any word for w with one letter deleted, with the exchange and deletion conditions as corollaries and the inversion sequence of a reduced word listing exactly the inversions of its element; TauCeti#2823 had this for Weyl groups from the geometry of positive roots, and this is the general case by the reflection cocycle, with Matsumoto's theorem the next milestone (Björner–Brenti, *Combinatorics of Coxeter Groups*, §1.4; Humphreys §5.8).
name: The strong exchange condition for Coxeter systems

about: the polytabloids of the standard Young tableaux of shape μ form a basis of the Specht module S^μ over ℚ, so dim S^μ = f^μ, the number of standard tableaux of shape μ; linear independence is triangularity in the dominance order and spanning is the straightening algorithm through the Garnir relations (James, *The Representation Theory of the Symmetric Groups*, §8; Sagan, *The Symmetric Group*, Thm 2.5.2).
name: The standard basis theorem for Specht modules

about: for K = ℚ(√d), d squarefree, real or imaginary, the 2-rank of the narrow class group Cl⁺(K) is exactly t − 1, t the number of ramified rational primes: the lower bound is the independence of the genus characters, every sign pattern of product one being realised by a degree-one prime from Dirichlet's theorem, and it closes the real case that the first-inequality bullet of TauCeti#4222 left open; the narrow ambiguous class number 2^(t−1) and |Gal(K_gen/K)| = |Cl⁺(K)/Cl⁺(K)²| for the narrow genus field follow (Lemmermeyer, *Reciprocity Laws*, §2.2; Cox, *Primes of the Form x² + ny²*, §6.A).
name: Gauss's 2-rank formula for quadratic fields of either signature

about: for a monic separable polynomial over a field of characteristic other than 2, the discriminant is a square in the base field exactly when the Galois group permutes the roots evenly, via σ(δ) = sign(σ)·δ for the root-difference product δ = ∏_{i<j}(rᵢ − rⱼ); in characteristic 2 every such discriminant is a square, so the test is vacuous there (Cohen, *A Course in Computational Algebraic Number Theory*, §6.3; Dummit–Foote §14.6).
name: The discriminant test for the alternating group
